body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §16.5.1 (pp. 374–375, printed) / IEEE 1800-2023 §16.5.1 (pp. 393–394, printed). Identical text in both editions.

**Normative requirement:** "The sampled value of a variable in a time slot corresponding to time 0 is its default sampled value." and "The default sampled value of a static variable is the value assigned in its declaration, or, in the absence of such an assignment, it is the default (or uninitialized) value of the corresponding type".

**Probes:** Slurm jobs 3751 and 3753, Icarus 13.0 devel cc25756d1, `-g2017` and `-g2023`, assertions enabled. Sources and raw logs: `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c16-20261021/attempt-01-sampling/followup-s3-timezero-outcome-20261021/` and `.../followup-d4-and-c16-controls-20261021/`. Common setup: `bit c0=0; initial #0 c0=1;` (posedge at time 0).
- S3d control: `assert property (@(posedge c0) 1'b0) else $display("S3d FAIL %0t",$time);` → `S3d FAIL 0` in both editions (an attempt does start at time 0).
- S3e: `logic v=0; initial v=1; assert property (@(posedge c0) v) $display("S3e PASS %0t",$time); else $display("S3e FAIL %0t",$time);` → **`S3e PASS 0`** in both editions.
- S3a (same `v`, fail action only) and S3b (`logic w; initial w=1;`, uninitialized, default sampled value `x`) → no failure reported in either edition.

**Expected:** at time 0 the sampled value of `v` is its declaration value 0, so S3e/S3a report `FAIL 0`; for S3b the sampled value is `1'bx`, so the assertion fails at 0. After time 0, Preponed sampling is correct (S1/S2/S5 fail exactly once at t=25 for an NBA- or blocking-updated counter), so the defect is specific to the time-0 rule.

**Impact:** assertions on reset/initialization behavior can pass vacuously at time 0 because they observe values written by `initial` blocks in the same time slot.
title: [IEEE 1800] §16.5.1 — Concurrent assertions at time 0 use the current value instead of the default sampled value

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §16.14.3 (p. 460, printed) / IEEE 1800-2023 §16.14.3 (p. 479, printed). Identical wording (action-control cross-reference 20.12 → 20.11).

**Normative requirement:** "The pass statement specified in statement_or_null shall be executed once for each successful evaluation attempt of the underlying property_spec. The pass statement shall be executed in the Reactive region of the time step in which the corresponding evaluation attempt succeeds."

**Probe:** `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c16-20261021/attempt-01-sampling/followup-d4-and-c16-controls-20261021/input/c16/s3c_default_sample_initialized_pass_control.sv` (Slurm job 3751, Icarus 13.0 devel cc25756d1, `-g2017` and `-g2023`, `-gassertions`):
```systemverilog
cover property (@(posedge c0) u) $display("S3c COVER %0t", $time);
```
**Observed (both editions):** compile emits `warning: the pass statement of this 'cover property' is not executed (recorded corner); it is dropped. The match counter still counts.`; at run time no `S3c COVER` line is printed although the clock edge occurs (`S3c EDGE 0`) and `u` is 1.
Source: `pform.cc` deletes `pass_stmt` for `kind == 2 && pass_stmt && prop->op_type != 3` (and in the checker-lowered path, `if (cover && pass_stmt)`), so this is not specific to the probe's time-0 edge.
Contrast: `assert property` pass actions do execute (`s7_concurrent_assert_pass_action_syntax.sv` prints PASS at 5/15/25/35/45 in both editions).

**Expected:** each successful attempt of a `cover property` executes its pass statement in the Reactive region. A warning does not substitute for the required behavior. (Matrix §16.14 is being downgraded from IMPLEMENTED to PARTIAL accordingly.)
title: [IEEE 1800] §16.14.3 — cover property pass statement is dropped at compile time (warning only); never executed

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §6.24.1 (pp. 132–133, printed; Syntax 6-7 `casting_type ::= … | const`) / IEEE 1800-2023 §6.24.1 (p. 140, printed). Identical text. Cross-reference: §16.5.1 (2017 p. 375 / 2023 p. 394) defines the sampled value of a `const` cast in assertions.

**Normative requirement:** "An expression may be changed to a constant with a const cast. `const'(x)` … the type of the expression to be cast shall pass through unchanged. The only effect is to treat the value as though it had been used to define a const variable".

**Probes:** Slurm job 3751, Icarus 13.0 devel cc25756d1, `-g2017` and `-g2023`, `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c16-20261021/attempt-01-sampling/followup-d4-and-c16-controls-20261021/input/c16/`:
- `s6_const_cast_general_expression_control.sv`: `int cnt=2; initial $display("S6 control const=%0d", const'(cnt));` → compile rc=2, syntax error, both editions.
- `s6_const_cast_assignment_control.sv` (const' on an assignment RHS) → compile rc=2, both editions.
- `s6_const_cast_uses_current_observed_value.sv`: `assert property (@(posedge clk) const'(cnt)!=2) else …` → rc=3, "syntax error … Error in property_spec of concurrent assertion item", both editions.
- Control `s6_type_cast_assignment_control.sv`: `int'(cnt)` compiles and prints 2, both editions, so the general cast path works; only the `const` casting_type is missing.

**Expected:** `const'(cnt)` parses wherever a cast is legal and yields `cnt`'s value with its type unchanged (control prints `const=2`). In a concurrent assertion its sampled value is the current value (§16.5.1), so with `cnt` incremented by NBA at each posedge the assertion `const'(cnt)!=2` fails once, at the second posedge.
title: [IEEE 1800] §6.24.1 — const'(expr) cast is a syntax error (also blocks §16.5.1/§16.14.6 const-cast sampling)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §14.16.2 (p. 353, printed) / IEEE 1800-2023 §14.16.2 (p. 371, printed). Identical wording in both editions.

**Normative requirement:** "It shall be illegal to write to a variable with a continuous assignment, a procedural continuous assignment, or a primitive when that variable is associated with an output clockvar."

**Probes:** `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c14-20261021/attempt-02-multidrive/input/` (Slurm job 3749, Icarus 13.0 devel cc25756d1, `-g2017` and `-g2023`). Each declares `logic q;` and `clocking cb @(posedge clk); output q; endclocking`, then:
- `n7a_continuous_assignment_to_clockvar_variable.sv`: `assign q = 0;`
- `n7b_primitive_to_clockvar_variable.sv`: `buf b(q, a);`
- `n7c_procedural_continuous_to_clockvar_variable.sv`: `initial assign q = 0;`

**Observed:** all three compile with rc=0 and no diagnostic in both editions.

**Related, not duplicates:** #908 covers blocking / regular intra-assignment-delay writes to the clockvar itself (`cb.q = …`, `cb.q <= #4 …`); a continuous assignment to the clockvar itself (`assign cb.q = …`) is already rejected. This issue is about writers of the *associated variable* `q`.
Controls in the same job pass: a plain procedural assignment to the associated variable holds until the next synchronous drive, as the standard permits (d8: `55` at 7, still `55` at 16, `aa` at 25).

**Expected:** a compile-time error for each of n7a, n7b and n7c in both editions.
title: [IEEE 1800] §14.16.2 — Continuous, primitive and procedural-continuous drivers of an output-clockvar variable are accepted (required error)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §14.16 (pp. 350–351) / IEEE 1800-2023 §14.16 (p. 369, printed). Same requirements in both editions.

**Normative requirement:** "It shall be an error to write to a clockvar except by using the synchronous drive syntax described in this subclause." and "No other form of intra-assignment delay syntax shall be legal in a synchronous drive to a clockvar."

**Probe:** `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c14-20261021/attempt-01-sync-drive-depth/`, cases N3 and N4 (Slurm job 3743), Icarus 13.0 devel cc25756d1, `-g2017` and `-g2023`.
- N3: `vif.cb.data = 8'h01;` (blocking assignment to a clockvar output)
- N4: `vif.cb.data <= #4 8'h01;` (regular intra-assignment delay; the standard's own example marks `bus.data <= #4 r;` as an error)

**Observed:** both compile with no diagnostic in both editions.
Control: N5, a continuous assignment to a clockvar (`assign top.bus.cb.data = 1;`), is correctly rejected, so the restriction exists only for continuous assignments.

**Expected:** compile-time errors for N3 and N4. Only `clockvar_expression <= [cycle_delay] expression` may write a clockvar. One issue because both are the same missing check: procedural writes to a clockvar are not restricted to the synchronous-drive form.
title: [IEEE 1800] §14.16 — Blocking assignment and regular intra-assignment delay to a clockvar are accepted (required error)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §14.12 (p. 344) with §14.11 (p. 343) / IEEE 1800-2023 §14.12 (p. 362, printed) with §14.11 (p. 361, printed). Wording identical for the cited sentences.

**Normative requirement:** §14.12: a default clocking's scope "includes … any nested modules … It does not include instantiated modules, interfaces, or checkers." §14.11: "If no default clocking has been specified for the current module, interface, checker, or program, then the compiler shall issue an error."

**Probe:** `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c14-20261021/attempt-01-sync-drive-depth/`, case N2 (Slurm job 3743), Icarus 13.0 devel cc25756d1, `-g2017` and `-g2023`.
Shape: a parent module declares `default clocking cb @(posedge clk); endclocking` and instantiates a separately declared child module; the child has no clocking declaration and executes `##1`.

**Observed:** compiles with no diagnostic in both editions.
Controls: a module with no default clocking anywhere is rejected (existing `n14_11_no_default_clocking.sv`); a module's own `default clocking` with `##3` resumes at the correct edge (case K9).

**Expected:** compile-time error in the child: default clocking does not propagate into instantiated modules, so `##1` there has no default clocking.
title: [IEEE 1800] §14.12 — ##N accepted in an instantiated module that inherits no default clocking (required error)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §14.16 (p. 350) / IEEE 1800-2023 §14.16 (pp. 368–369, printed). Wording identical except 2023 spells `cycle_delay` as `## integral_number | ## identifier | ## ( expression )`; `##2` is legal in both.

**Normative requirement:** "updating of the target signal shall be postponed for the specified number of cycles of the target clockvar's clocking block, plus any clocking output skew specified for that clockvar." The drive "shall not cause execution of the statement to block."

**Probe:** `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c14-20261021/attempt-01-sync-drive-depth/`, case K3 (Slurm job 3743), Icarus 13.0 devel cc25756d1, `-g2017` and `-g2023`.
Shape: interface `bus_if` with `clocking cb @(posedge clk); default input #1step output #0; output data; ... endclocking`; a class holding `virtual bus_if vif` executes `@(vif.cb); vif.cb.data <= ##2 8'h3C; $display("after %0t",$time);`.

**Observed:** compilation fails in both editions with `this nonblocking property assignment form is not yet supported without changing its NBA semantics`.
Control (Slurm job 3746): the same drive through a direct hierarchical reference `top.bus.cb.data <= ##2 8'h3C` compiles and runs correctly in both editions (prints `after 5` at the drive, data changes at the clocking event two cycles later, final value 3C). The failure is therefore specific to the virtual-interface clockvar path.
Zero-cycle virtual-interface drives (`vif.cb.data <= v`, output skew, slice drives) pass (cases K1, K2, K4).

**Expected:** the virtual-interface form compiles and behaves like the direct form: statement does not block; `data` becomes 3C at the second subsequent `cb` clocking event (+ output skew). This is the standard UVM driver idiom (`vif.cb.sig <= ##N v`).
title: [IEEE 1800] §14.16 — Cycle-delayed synchronous drive through a virtual-interface clockvar fails codegen

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §13.5.3 (p.332); IEEE 1800-2023 §13.5.3 (p.350). Same text in both editions.

**Normative requirement:** "The default_expression is evaluated in the scope containing the subroutine declaration each time a call using the default is made." The formals belong to the subroutine's own scope, so a default expression cannot refer to an earlier formal. A name in the default resolves in the scope containing the declaration.

**Probes** (Slurm job 3737, audit toolchain cc25756d1 — frontend/elaboration unchanged through origin/main 10f3a0a — -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c13-20261021/attempt-01-default-args/):
```systemverilog
module p13_d7; int a = 100;
  function int k(input int a = 1, input int b = a + 1); return b; endfunction
  initial $display("D7 %0d", k());
endmodule
```
- With module-scope `a = 100`: prints **2** (the formal a was used). Expected **101**.
- Without any enclosing `a`: accepted, prints **2**. Expected a compile error (unresolved `a` in the containing scope).

**Controls (pass in both editions):** an input default (5); a `= null` class-handle default; an explicitly empty named argument `f(.a())` takes the default; and the package-scope probe D9, where a default declared in a package uses the package's `gv` (27), not the caller's `gv` (99), which shows correct declaration-scope evaluation for non-formal names.

**Expected:** `D7 101` with the outer `a`, and a compile error without it, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed search over all 408 issues for 'default expression scope', 'earlier formal default', 'default argument declaration scope', 'formal default expression', 'subroutine declaration scope': no match. Related but distinct: #633 (output/inout defaults unsupported), #703 (ref defaults rejected).
title: [IEEE 1800] §13.5.3 — default argument expression is evaluated in the subroutine's own scope (sees earlier formals) instead of the declaration's containing scope

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §21.4 / §21.4.1 (p.647); IEEE 1800-2023 §21.4 / §21.4.1. Quote (identical in both editions): "When loading dynamic arrays and queues, the current size of the array is fixed; the array shall not be resized." Loading dynamic arrays and queues is therefore legal; their size is kept. $writememh/$writememb (§21.5) apply to the same memory kinds.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c21/p21_04b_dynqueue.sv (Slurm job 3717, audit toolchain main-cc25756; vvp/vvp_readmem.c unchanged through origin/main 10f3a0; -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c21-20261021/attempt-02-dynqueue/{RESULT.md,STANDARD.md,DEDUPE.md}). A dynamic array and a queue, each preallocated to 2 elements, are loaded from a 3-word file, then the dynamic array is written back with $writememh and re-read.

Observed in both editions: compile succeeds, then the run exits 1 with four errors. $readmemh rejects the dynamic array (line 6), $readmemh rejects the queue (line 7), $writememh rejects the dynamic array (line 8), and the following $readmemh rejects it again. No result line is printed.

**Expected:** the first two words load into each container, both sizes remain 2 (a warning about the extra word is acceptable), and $writememh writes the dynamic array so the round trip matches, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'readmemh dynamic array queue', 'readmem queue', '21.4.1 dynamic array queue', 'readmemb queue' returned no issues. #803 (open) covers associative arrays only.
title: [IEEE 1800] §21.4/§21.4.1 — $readmemh/$writememh reject dynamic arrays and queues at run time

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §7.8.6; IEEE 1800-2023 §7.8.6.

**Normative requirement:** an associative-array index expression containing x or z bits is invalid. A write through an invalid index shall be ignored and a warning issued. A read of a nonexistent entry returns the Table 7-1 default with a warning.

**Probe** (Slurm job 3251, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c07-20261019/attempt-11-invalid-associative-index-rerun/README.md; archive SHA256 f110fc55…):
- Control (passes): a read of a missing entry in a 2-state `int` associative array returns 0, does not allocate an entry, and prints the required nonexistent-entry warning. That is the fix from closed #486.
- Gap: a write through the key `4'bx001` **allocates an entry** in both editions, and **no invalid-write warning** is issued. stderr contains only the earlier missing-read warning.

**Expected:** the write is ignored (num()/exists unchanged) and a warning is issued, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'associative invalid index', '7.8.6'. Closed #486 covers the nonexistent-entry *read* warning only. #853 (struct-key crash) and #484 (fixed-array elements) are distinct.
title: [IEEE 1800] §7.8.6 — associative-array write with an X/Z index allocates an entry instead of being ignored with a warning

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §32.5 (multiple annotations), with §32.6 (multiple SDF files); IEEE 1800-2023 same. Citations: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c32-20261021/attempt-05-label-order-multi/STANDARD.md.

**Normative requirement:** SDF constructs are applied in file order. A later INCREMENT construct *modifies* (adds to) the previously annotated value, while a later ABSOLUTE *overwrites* it. Across multiple $sdf_annotate calls (§32.6), later files likewise modify (INCREMENT) or overwrite (ABSOLUTE) earlier annotations.

**Probes** (Slurm job 3712, audit toolchain from source cc25756d — SDF sources unchanged through origin/main 10f3a0a — -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify; zero SDF ERROR/WARNING; off-edge sampling; raw logs …/raw-slurm/final-3712-logs/):
- Same CELL, `(DELAY (ABSOLUTE (IOPATH a y (4) (6))))` then `(DELAY (INCREMENT (IOPATH a y (1) (1))))`: rise/fall **1/1**. Expected 5/7.
- Reversed order (INCREMENT 1/1, then ABSOLUTE 4/6): 4/6. This is correct, but only because ABSOLUTE overwrites.
- §32.6 with three $sdf_annotate calls scoped to u1, u2, u1, where the third file is INCREMENT 1/1 on u1 after ABSOLUTE 4/6: u1 gets **1/1** (expected 5/7). u2 gets 7/9, so scope isolation is correct.

The INCREMENT value replaces the delay instead of being added to it, and no warning is issued, so the annotated timing is silently wrong.

**Expected:** 5/7 for the same-file and multi-file increment cases, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed search across all 404 issues (evidence DEDUPE.md, dedupe-search.json). No §32.5/§32.6 or INCREMENT match. #880 (PATHPULSE), #898 (TIMINGCHECK) and #899 (mtm/scale arguments) are distinct.
title: [IEEE 1800] §32.5 — SDF INCREMENT is applied as an absolute replacement (ABSOLUTE 4/6 then INCREMENT 1/1 gives 1/1, expected 5/7), silently

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §32.4.3 (and the §32.4 cell grammar: a CELL may contain DELAY, TIMINGCHECK and LABEL sections), §32.3 (an annotator warns about data it cannot annotate); IEEE 1800-2023 same. Citations: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c32-20261021/attempt-05-label-order-multi/STANDARD.md.

**Normative requirement:** an SDF LABEL section annotates specparam values, and expressions that use those specparams (e.g., module path delays) are re-evaluated with the annotated values.

**Probes** (Slurm job 3712, audit toolchain from source cc25756d — SDF sources unchanged through origin/main 10f3a0a — -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify; raw logs: …/raw-slurm/final-3712-logs/):
- `specify specparam tr = 1, tf = 1; (a => y) = (tr, tf); endspecify`, with `(CELL (CELLTYPE "d1") (INSTANCE u1) (LABEL (ABSOLUTE (tr 4) (tf 6))))` (the standard's syntax). Both editions print three `SDF ERROR` lines (syntax error in CELL; invalid DELAYFILE format), no SDF WARNING, and the path delay stays 1/1. Expected 4/6.
- Mixed file: DELAY (IOPATH 4/6) followed by LABEL in the same CELL. The IOPATH 4/6 is kept, but the same three errors are reported for the standards-valid LABEL section.
- Control: the same cell and scope with IOPATH only gives 4/6 and no diagnostics.

**Root cause evidence:** vpi/sdf_parse.y has timing_spec productions only for DELAY and TIMINGCHECK; vpi/sdf_lexor.lex has no LABEL token (excerpt: …/parser-source.txt).

**Expected:** LABEL ABSOLUTE/INCREMENT sections parse, and the specparams and dependent path delays are updated (4/6 here), in both editions. Where a label cannot be applied, §32.3 requires a warning for that data, not a syntax error against a valid file.

**Dedupe:** open+closed search across all 404 issues (evidence DEDUPE.md, dedupe-search.json). No §32.4.3 match. #19 (closed) and #822 (open) cover unrelated specparam contexts; #880, #898 and #899 are distinct SDF gaps.
title: [IEEE 1800] §32.4.3 — SDF LABEL sections are not supported: the parser rejects standards-valid files (SDF ERROR, specparams not annotated)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §32.9 (Syntax 32-1, Tables 32-5/32-6); IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** $sdf_annotate's optional mtm_spec (MAXIMUM / MINIMUM / TYPICAL / TOOL_CONTROL, default TOOL_CONTROL) selects which min:typ:max value is annotated. scale_factors and scale_type (default FROM_MTM) scale the selected values.

**Probes** (Slurm job 3706, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify; zero 'SDF ERROR'; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c32-20261021/attempt-03-remaining/):
- p32_mtm.sv + .sdf: `(IOPATH a y (1:2:3) (4:5:6))`, annotated in separate runs with mtm_spec "MINIMUM", "TYPICAL" and "MAXIMUM". Each run warns `currently only uses the first two argument`, and every run shows rise 2 / fall 5. Expected 1/4, 2/5, 3/6.
- p32_scale.sv + .sdf: scale_factors "2.0:2.0:2.0", scale_type "FROM_TYPICAL". Same warning; rise 2 / fall 5 retained. Expected 4/10.

**Expected:** mtm_spec selects the min, typ or max value, and scale_factors/scale_type scale it, in both editions. The arguments are currently warned about and ignored.

**Controls (pass):** basic two-argument IOPATH annotation (rise 4 / fall 6, earlier job 3667); SDF INTERCONNECT delay 3 (Y at t13).

**Dedupe:** complete open+closed snapshots (275/127) searched for SDF, annotation, scale factors/type, mtm, delay path. Only #880 (§32.7 PATHPULSE) and the companion §32.4.2 TIMINGCHECK issue are related; neither covers the optional $sdf_annotate arguments.
title: [IEEE 1800] §32.9 — $sdf_annotate ignores mtm_spec, scale_factors and scale_type ('currently only uses the first two argument')

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §32.4.2 (Table 32-2, SDF timing-check → SystemVerilog timing-check mapping, e.g. SETUP → $setup); IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** SDF TIMINGCHECK entries annotate the limits of the matching specify-block timing checks (SETUP → $setup / setup limit of $setuphold, HOLD, RECOVERY, …).

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c32/p32_tchk.sv + p32_tchk.sdf (Slurm job 3706, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify; zero 'SDF ERROR' lines; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c32-20261021/attempt-03-remaining/, raw-slurm/logs/):
- Source: `$setup(d, posedge clk, 1, notifier)`. SDF: `(TIMINGCHECK (SETUP d (posedge clk) (5)))`. Data changes 3 units before the clock edge.
- Annotated run: `SDF WARNING: … TIMINGCHECK not supported.`, and **no violation** (expected one, since 3 < 5).
- Unannotated control: no violation (correct, since 3 > 1).

The §32.3 warning is issued, so this is reported honestly, but the annotation itself is absent.

**Expected:** the SETUP limit becomes 5, and the probe reports one $setup violation, in both editions. The other Table 32-2 mappings are required as well.

**Dedupe:** complete open+closed snapshots (275/127) searched for SDF, specify, setup/setuphold, annotation, TIMINGCHECK. Related but distinct: #880 (§32.7 PATHPULSE), #890 (§31.9 negative checks), #891/#892 (§31.4 skew checks).
title: [IEEE 1800] §32.4.2 — SDF TIMINGCHECK annotation is not supported (SETUP limit not applied; 'TIMINGCHECK not supported')

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §6.6.7/§6.22 (nettype matching: a nettype matches only itself or its declared alias) and §23.3.3 (port connection rules for user-defined nettypes); IEEE 1800-2023 same. Text and pages: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c06j-20261020/README.md.

**Normative requirement:** a port of a user-defined nettype may only be connected to a net of a matching nettype. Two separately declared nettypes with the same data type (and resolution function) are distinct, not matching. Only a nettype alias declared with `nettype old_t new_t;` matches.

**Probe** (pinned audit toolchain, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c06j-20261020/): a nettype and its declared alias connect and run through a user-defined-nettype port, which passes. A net of a second, separately declared nettype with the same data type is also accepted on that port, with no diagnostic in either edition.

**Expected:** a compile-time error for the distinct-nettype connection, in both editions. The alias connection stays legal.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches for clauses 6.22.3/6.22.4/6.22.6/23.3.3, nettype ports, aliases, same-data-type nettypes (evidence dedupe-results-full.txt, dedupe-live-20261020.txt) and 'nettype'. Only #435 (class-method resolution functions for nettypes) and #474/#492 matched; none covers nettype matching on ports.
title: [IEEE 1800] §6.22/§23.3.3 — port connection between two distinct user-defined nettypes with the same data type is accepted

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §16.13.5 and §16.13.6; IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** a named sequence's `.matched` method may be used in a sequence or property clocked by a different clock. The endpoint detected on the source clock is synchronized to the first subsequent tick of the destination clock.

**Probe** (Slurm jobs 3584–3586, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c16e-20261020/README.md, draft candidate-issue-draft.md): a minimal legal cross-clock use of `source_seq.matched` fails to elaborate in both editions with `Unable to bind wire/reg/memory 'source_seq.matched' in 'main'`. Runtime is not reached.

**Control (pass):** same-clock `.matched` (tests/sva_nfa/endpoint_triggered.sv) compiles and runs in both editions with the expected `EP_FAIL@55` and `endpoint_cover=2`.

**Expected:** the cross-clock use elaborates, and the endpoint is observed on the first destination-clock tick after the source match, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches '16.13.5', 'matched multiclock', 'matched', 'sequence method', 'matched clock'. #653 (.triggered in wait, §9.4.4) and #719 (subroutine calls in match items) are different behaviors. Open #446 covers multiclock antecedent handoff/multiplicity semantics, not .matched binding across clocks, so this is filed separately.
title: [IEEE 1800] §16.13.5/§16.13.6 — cross-clock sequence .matched fails elaboration (Unable to bind 'source_seq.matched')

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §23.5 (extern modules); IEEE 1800-2023 §23.5.

**Normative requirement:** `extern module` declarations (non-ANSI and ANSI, including parameter port lists) declare a module's interface separately from its body, so that the module can be referenced (and its body declared with `.*` ports) consistently.

**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c23/p23_04b_extern_m.sv and p23_04c_extern_param.sv (pinned audit toolchain, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c23d-20261020/attempt-03/README.md). Both fail at the `extern` token with a syntax error in both editions; no runtime is reached.

**Expected:** both extern module forms are accepted, and the subsequent module definition (including the `.*` port-list form) matches the extern declaration, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'extern module', '23.5'. Hits #824 (extern forkjoin in interfaces, §25.7.4), #841/#842 (external constraint blocks), #823 (modport task export) and #641 (out-of-class extern function) are distinct.
title: [IEEE 1800] §23.5 — extern module declarations (non-ANSI and parameterized ANSI) are syntax errors at the extern keyword

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §23.4 (nested modules); IEEE 1800-2023 §23.4.

**Normative requirement:** a module declaration may be nested inside another module. The nested module is visible only within its enclosing module, may be instantiated there, and can reference names from the enclosing scope.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c23/p23_04f_nested_module_scope.sv (pinned audit toolchain, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c23d-20261020/attempt-02/README.md). A module `inner` is declared inside the outer module, instantiated in the same scope, and reads an enclosing variable. Elaboration fails in both editions with `Unknown module type: inner`; no runtime is reached.

**Expected:** the nested module instantiates and resolves the enclosing-scope reference, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'nested module', '23.4' (plus the runner's searches in the evidence) found no matching issue; hits #672, #478, #473, #497, #499, #434, #103, #27 are unrelated.
title: [IEEE 1800] §23.4 — nested module declared and instantiated in the same scope fails: "Unknown module type: inner"

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §29.8 (UDP instances) with Syntax 29-? / Annex A udp_instance → name_of_instance ::= instance_identifier { unpacked_dimension }; IEEE 1800-2023 same. Text checked directly in both PDFs (evidence README).

**Normative requirement:** a UDP instance may be declared as an array of instances (an instance name with an unpacked range), with the same connection rules as gate arrays.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c29/p29_instance_array.sv (Slurm jobs 3692/3693, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c29-20261021/attempt-02-udp-more/ and attempt-03-*/):
```systemverilog
latchff ua[1:0](qv, clk, d, clr);   // qv is wire [1:0]
```
Compile fails in both editions with `UDPs with a range (ua [1:0]) are not supported.`

**Controls (pass in both editions):** a named single instance, an unnamed instance, and a two-value delay `#(2,3)` compile and simulate correctly. Three delay values are rejected (`UDPs take at most two delay arguments.`), as required. A mixed level/edge sequential table produces the expected output.

**Expected:** the array instantiates two UDPs (ua[1], ua[0]) whose bit-sliced or replicated connections follow the array-of-instances rules, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'UDP instance', 'UDP delay', 'level-sensitive dominance', '29.8', '29.10' found no existing issue (evidence DEDUPE.md).
title: [IEEE 1800] §29.8 — UDP instance arrays (latchff ua[1:0](...)) are rejected: "UDPs with a range … are not supported"

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §31.4.2 and §31.4.3 (Tables 31-8/31-9); IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** $timeskew and $fullskew accept optional event_based_flag and remain_active_flag arguments (constant expressions). event_based_flag switches the check to event-based reporting; remain_active_flag changes dormancy/second-timestamp behavior.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c31/ K3 `$timeskew(posedge a3, posedge b3, 2, , 1)` (Slurm jobs 3690/3691, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c31-20261021/attempt-04-skew-timer/). Compile exits 1 in both editions:
`sorry: $timeskew event_based/remain_active flag arguments are not supported; the check is dropped.`

**Expected:** the flags are accepted. With event_based_flag=1 and no data event, no violation is reported; with a late data event, the report comes at that event. remain_active_flag behaves per the table. Both editions.

**Note:** the explicit 'sorry' and compile failure are honest, but legal source cannot compile. The default (no-flag) timer-based mode is also absent; that is filed separately.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches '$timeskew', '$fullskew', 'timer-based', 'event_based_flag'. Only #890 (negative timing checks) and the companion default-mode issue match; neither covers flag acceptance.
title: [IEEE 1800] §31.4.2/§31.4.3 — $timeskew/$fullskew event_based_flag and remain_active_flag arguments are rejected and the check is dropped

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §31.4.2 and §31.4.3 (Tables 31-8/31-9); IEEE 1800-2023 same. Excerpts: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c31-20261021/attempt-04-skew-timer/STANDARD.md.

**Normative requirement:** "The default behavior for $timeskew is timer-based." / "The default behavior for $fullskew is timer-based." In timer-based mode a violation is reported as soon as the elapsed time since the reference (timestamp) event exceeds the limit, without waiting for a data event. Only event_based_flag switches this to event-based reporting.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c31/p31_skewtimer*.sv (Slurm jobs 3690/3691, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify; raw logs in the evidence directory):
- K1 `$timeskew(posedge a1, posedge b1, 2)`, a1 rises at t10, b1 never rises: **no report** (expected one report at about t12–t13).
- K2 the same, but b1 rises at t30: report **only at t30** (expected about t12–t13).
- K4 `$fullskew(posedge a4, posedge b4, 2, 2)`, a4 rises at t50, b4 never rises: **no report** (expected one at about t52–t53).
- C0 `$skew` control with no data event: no report (correct; $skew is event-based).

Both editions are identical. Under the default (no flags), $timeskew and $fullskew therefore behave event-based.

**Expected:** under the default, K1 and K4 each report once at the limit expiry, and K2 reports at expiry rather than at t30. Both editions.

**Related:** the optional event_based_flag/remain_active_flag arguments are rejected with a 'sorry'; that is filed separately. Earlier Clause 31 probes where the data event coincided with expiry at 1-unit precision could not distinguish the two modes.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches '$timeskew', '$fullskew', 'timer-based', 'event_based_flag'. Only #890 matched, and it cites these checks as positive-limit controls in the negative-timing-check issue; it does not cover the reporting mode.
title: [IEEE 1800] §31.4.2/§31.4.3 — $timeskew and $fullskew are evaluated event-based; the required default timer-based reporting is absent

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §31.9 and §31.9.1 (pp.887–889); IEEE 1800-2023 §31.9 and §31.9.1. Excerpts: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c31-20261021/attempt-03-tchk3/STANDARD.md.

**Normative requirements:**
- $setuphold and $recrem accept negative values "when the negative timing check option is enabled".
- §31.9.1 a: a violation is triggered only for a change inside the shifted violation window, exclusive of the end points.
- §31.9.1 b: "The value of the latched data shall be the one that is stable during the violation window."
- Delayed copies of the data and reference signals are generated, and explicit delayed signals can be declared and used by the model. If an adjusted limit becomes <= 0 it is set to 0 with a warning.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c31/p31_neg.sv (Slurm job 3689, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify; evidence above):
```systemverilog
always @(posedge dclk) q <= dd;
specify $setuphold(posedge clk, d, -2, 6, notifier, , , dclk, dd); endspecify
// A: clk rises at 10, d changes at 11 (before window (12,16)) -> expect no violation, q latches 1
// B: clk rises at 40, d changes at 44 (inside window (42,46)) -> expect exactly one violation
```
Observed in both editions: a hold violation at t11 and `A q=0 nc=1` (expected `q=1 nc=0`); then a hold violation at t44 and `B nc=2` (expected 1 violation total). iverilog/vvp help and man pages expose no negative-timing-check option; `-gneg_tchk` is rejected (`Unknown/Unsupported Language generation neg_tchk`). No clamp warning is issued.

**Expected:** a way to enable negative timing checks; the shifted window (12,16) and (42,46); dclk/dd delayed so that q latches the value stable during the window; exactly one violation (B). Both editions.

**Controls (pass in both editions):** positive-limit $setuphold, $recrem, $setup/$hold/$width/$period/$skew/$nochange, edge-control specifiers, &&& conditions and vector signals all report correctly with -gspecify.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches '$recrem', '$timeskew', '$fullskew', '&&&', 'edge control', 'negative timing check', 'delayed signal' each returned none (evidence DEDUPE.md).
title: [IEEE 1800] §31.9 — negative timing checks unsupported: no enabling option, negative $setuphold limits produce spurious violations and delayed signals latch the wrong data

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §37.17 (variables), §38.23 (vpi_iterate traverses all associated objects); IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** the VPI object model exposes the declared objects of a design. Nothing in Clause 37 permits omitting a declared variable because it is never read. vpi_iterate shall traverse all objects of the requested type associated with the reference object.

**Probe** (Slurm job 3687, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c37-20261021/attempt-02-var-scope/):
- p37_var_unref.sv (`logic [7:0] v;` never used): `vpi_iterate(vpiReg, p37)` returns only y.
- p37_reg.sv (`reg [7:0] v;` never used): the same, only y.
- p37_var_ref.sv (identical, but v is read by an initial $display): vpiReg returns v (size 8) and y (size 4).

Visibility depends on whether the variable is referenced, which suggests unused declarations are optimized away before VPI object creation.

**Expected:** v is reachable through VPI (vpiReg / vpiVariables, and vpi_handle_by_name) whether or not it is referenced, in both editions. If an optimization is applied, it must not remove VPI-visible objects (or must be an explicit opt-in mode).

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'vpiVariables', 'unused variable VPI', 'vpiInstance', 'vpiScope module', 'vpiModule parent' returned no matching issue (evidence DEDUPE.md). The empty vpiVariables iteration is filed separately.
title: [IEEE 1800] §37.17/§38.23 — declared but unreferenced variables are not visible through VPI iteration (vpiReg omits unused logic/reg v)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §40.5.3 (p.1130), §38.6 (p.1056), §38.2 (p.1052); IEEE 1800-2023 §40.5.2 (p.1166), §38.6 (p.1092), §38.2 (p.1088).

**Normative requirements:**
- §40.5.3 (2023 §40.5.2): `vpi_get(<coverageType>, instance_handle)` "returns the number of covered items of the given coverage type in the given instance." No special return is defined for an unavailable coverage type.
- §38.6: "Should an error occur, vpi_get() shall return vpiUndefined."
- §38.2: vpi_chk_error returns an error severity if the previous VPI routine call resulted in an error, and 0 otherwise.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c40/vpi_cov.c + p40.sv (Slurm job 3682, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c40-20261021/attempt-01-vpi-cov/):
- `vpi_get(vpiToggleCoverage /* Annex K 763, guarded fallback */, p40)` returns **-1** (vpiUndefined).
- The immediately following `vpi_chk_error()` returns **0** (no error recorded).

**Why it is a gap:** -1 is only meaningful as the §38.6 error return. Returning it while vpi_chk_error reports no error is inconsistent: an application cannot tell whether -1 is a count, an error, or 'no coverage'. Code coverage is not instrumented in this simulator, so the conforming options are to return a defined count (e.g., 0 covered items) or to return vpiUndefined *and* record an error retrievable through vpi_chk_error, with a message stating that the coverage type is unavailable.

**Controls (pass in both editions):** vpi_control(vpiCoverageCheck / vpiCoverageStart, vpiToggleCoverage, p40) returns 0 = SV_COV_NOCOV per §40.3.2.1 / Table 40-1, and $coverage_control/$coverage_get return SV_COV_NOCOV (job 3547).

**Severity:** low. This is error-reporting consistency, not fabricated coverage data.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'vpiCoverageStart', 'vpiCoverageCheck', 'coverage VPI', '40.5', 'coverage control', 'toggle coverage', 'code coverage VPI' (evidence DEDUPE.md). #883 (Annex M constants), #885 (Annex K missing names) and #443 (deferred-cover accounting) do not cover this.
title: [IEEE 1800] §38.6/§38.2/§40.5 — vpi_get(vpiToggleCoverage, module) returns vpiUndefined but vpi_chk_error reports no error

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 Annex K (normative vpi_user.h); IEEE 1800-2023 Annex K.

**Normative requirement:** Annex K is the normative vpi_user.h. Applications written against it expect every name it defines to be present with the listed value.

**Probe** (evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-annexKM-20261021/attempt-01-header-diff/{comparison.txt,RESULT.md,README.md}. Macro maps come from preprocessing the pinned audit toolchain headers built from source SHA fb584a251 with Apple Clang 21.0.3. Annex K #defines are extracted from both PDFs; page ranges are in README):
- Annex K 2017: 452 names, **0 value mismatches**, **257 standard names missing** from the installed vpi_user.h, 1 Icarus-only name.
- Annex K 2023: 455 names, 0 value mismatches, **260 missing** (adds vpiInterconnect, vpiNettypeNet, vpiNettypeNetSelect), 1 Icarus-only name.
- A C compile probe that uses the standard names `vpiAlways`, `cbAssign` and `vpiWidth` fails exactly on those three (#error assertions; exit 1).
- The full missing-name list is in comparison.txt.

**Scope note:** this is a public-header/ABI conformance gap. A missing name does not by itself prove the runtime lacks the behavior. Some constants may be omitted because the runtime does not implement the corresponding objects or properties, and those should be traced to their clause rows separately. The values that are present all match Annex K.

**Expected:** the installed vpi_user.h defines every Annex K name with its Annex K value (with any 2023 additions), so that standard VPI applications compile. Unsupported object types or properties are then reported at run time per Clause 38 (e.g., null handles or vpi_chk_error), not as compile failures in user code.

**Related:** #883 tracks the Annex M (sv_vpi_user.h) value mismatches (vpiAssertion, vpiModport) and the Annex M missing names.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'vpi_user.h', 'sv_vpi_user.h', 'Annex K', 'Annex M', 'VPI constant', 'vpiAlways', 'cbAssign', 'vpiWidth', 'standard VPI header', 'missing VPI constants'. Closed #502 is a false positive (fixed-array bug); #883/#884 cover Annex M / §39 only.
title: [IEEE 1800] Annex K — installed vpi_user.h omits 257 (2017) / 260 (2023) standard names (e.g., vpiAlways, cbAssign, vpiWidth)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §39.5.2 (assertion control through vpi_control), Annex K constants; IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** `vpi_control(vpiAssertionDisable, assertion_handle)` disables the assertion, so new attempts do not start and success/failure callbacks do not fire. Enable, reset, kill and the other Annex K assertion-control operations are defined alongside it.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c39/p39_dis.sv + vpi_assert.c (Slurm job 3674, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c39-20261021/attempt-01-assert-api/). `pa: assert property (@(posedge clk) a);` is disabled at time 0 with `vpi_control(620 /* Annex K vpiAssertionDisable */, pa)`:
- vpi_control returns 0, and stderr prints `Unsupported VPI control operation 620.`
- The cbAssertionFailure and cbAssertionSuccess counters still reach 2 and 2.

(The Icarus header has no vpiAssertionDisable symbol, so the probe uses a guarded fallback of 620 from Annex K. The header mismatch is a separate issue.)

**Controls (pass in both editions):** vpi_iterate over assertions finds `p39.pa` (with the Icarus value 686), and vpi_register_assertion_cb success/failure callbacks fire 2/2 as expected (§39.4.2).

**Expected:** after the disable, failures = 0 and successes = 0, and vpi_control returns success, in both editions. The other §39.5.2 control operations (enable, reset, kill, …) are required as well.

**Dedupe:** same open+closed search set as the companion Annex K issue (evidence DEDUPE.md). No relevant issue.
title: [IEEE 1800] §39.5.2 — VPI assertion control (vpi_control(vpiAssertionDisable, …)) is unsupported; callbacks keep firing

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 Annex K (sv_vpi_user.h) with §39.3.1; IEEE 1800-2023 Annex K with §39.3.1. No edition numbering difference.

**Normative requirement:** Annex K is the normative sv_vpi_user.h. It defines `#define vpiAssertion 744` and `#define vpiAssertionDisable 620` (with the other assertion-control constants). Applications compiled against the standard header must interoperate with the simulator's VPI.

**Observed** (evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c39-20261021/attempt-01-assert-api/, header syntax check attached; Slurm job 3674, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023):
- The installed Icarus `sv_vpi_user.h` defines `vpiAssertion` as **686** and has no `vpiAssertionDisable`.
- `vpi_iterate(686, NULL)` (the Icarus value) returns `p39.pa`. `vpi_iterate(744, NULL)` (the Annex K value) returns no assertions.

**Impact:** a VPI/assertion application built with the standard Annex K header cannot enumerate assertions on this simulator, and one built with the Icarus header is not portable.

**Expected:** sv_vpi_user.h constants match Annex K exactly, and the runtime accepts the Annex K values. This issue covers the header and constant ABI only. The missing implementation of assertion control through vpi_control (§39.5.2) is filed separately. A full audit of the remaining sv_vpi_user.h constants against Annex K is recommended as part of the fix.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'vpiAssertion', 'vpi_register_assertion_cb', 'cbAssertionFailure', 'vpiAssertionDisable', '39.', 'vpiAssertion 744', 'VPI assertion', 'assertion control VPI', 'assertion API' (evidence DEDUPE.md). Only unrelated #27 and #744 (closed).
title: [IEEE 1800] Annex M / §39.3.1 — sv_vpi_user.h assertion constants differ from the standard (vpiAssertion = 686, standard 744; vpiAssertionDisable missing)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §22.11.1 (protect is a standard pragma, specified in Clause 34), §34.3, §34.3.2, §34.5.3; IEEE 1800-2023 same. Quotes and pages: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c34-20261021/attempt-01-protect/README.md.

**Normative requirement:** tools perform envelope decryption when the proper key is supplied (§34.3). A tool supporting decrypting compilation transforms each decryption envelope (§34.3.2) and accumulates the pragmas of a begin_protected block (§34.5.3). The standard defines no fallback for a non-decrypting tool, and the §22.11 'unrecognized pragma → no effect' rule does not clearly apply, because `protect` is a standard pragma.

**Probes** (Slurm job 3671, pinned audit toolchain built from source SHA fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence above):
- tests/1800_audit/c34/p34_plain.sv: an unencrypted `pragma protect begin/end region compiles and prints `PLAIN`. This passes.
- tests/1800_audit/c34/n34_cipher.sv: the standard's raw x-caesar (rot13) begin_protected example. Compile exits 7 with `warning: macro centzn undefined (and assumed null)`, then syntax errors / invalid module instantiation at lines 7–19. The data block is parsed as SystemVerilog source. No diagnostic says that protected envelopes or decryption are unsupported.

**Expected:** either (a) decryption support for at least the standard-defined encoding/encryption examples, or (b) at minimum a clear diagnostic that identifies the begin_protected envelope as unsupported, instead of a cascade of misleading syntax errors from treating ciphertext as source. Both editions.

**Severity note:** decryption is a capability attached to decrypting tools and key exchange is tool-specific, so this is recorded as UNSUPPORTED. The misleading diagnostics are the honesty concern.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'pragma protect', 'protected envelope', 'begin_protected', '34.'. Only unrelated broad hits (#749, #803, #795).
title: [IEEE 1800] Clause 34 — protected envelopes: begin_protected blocks are parsed as source text (no decryption, no protected-envelope diagnostic)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §33.4 (§33.4.1 Syntax 33-4; §33.4.1.1 design statement; §33.4.1.3 instance selection; §33.4.1.5 liblist; §33.4.1.6 use binding); IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** a config declaration names the top-level design cells (`design`), the default library search order (`default liblist`), and per-instance bindings (`instance … use`) that replace the default cell binding.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c33/p33_cfg.sv (source SHA256 f695211a…; Slurm job 3668, current main fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c33-20261021/attempt-01-config/, raw slurm-3668-logs/):
```systemverilog
config cfg; design work.top; default liblist work; instance top.u use work.alt; endconfig
module top; leaf u(); endmodule
module leaf; initial $display("LEAF"); endmodule
module alt;  initial $display("ALT");  endmodule
```
With `-s cfg` and with `-s top`, in both editions: `p33_cfg.sv:1: sorry: config declarations (library-based cell binding) are not supported; remove the config block or select the implementation with plain module names.` (`-s cfg` is only the Icarus invocation; the standard does not define command-line selection.)

**Expected:** with the configuration selected, `top.u` binds to `alt` and prints `ALT`, in both editions. Without the configuration the default binding prints `LEAF`. The refusal is explicit, but the whole clause is unavailable.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'config', 'configuration', 'liblist', '33.' found no Clause 33 issue (evidence DEDUPE.md).
title: [IEEE 1800] Clause 33 — config declarations are not supported (sorry: config declarations … are not supported)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §32.7 (pulse limit annotation), §30.7 (pulse outcome rules), §32.3 (annotator shall warn for data it cannot annotate); IEEE 1800-2023 same subclauses.

**Normative requirement:** an SDF PATHPULSE entry annotates the reject and error limits of the matching module path (§32.7). Per §30.7, a pulse of width w with reject <= w < error produces x on the output, w < reject is rejected, and w >= error propagates. Under §32.3, data that cannot be annotated must be reported with a warning.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c32/p32_pp.sv + p32_pp.sdf (Slurm job 3667, current main fb584a251, -g2017 and -g2023 with -gspecify, zero 'SDF ERROR' lines; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c32-20261021/attempt-02-sdf-fixed/):
```
(DELAY (ABSOLUTE (IOPATH a y (4) (4))) (PATHPULSE a y (2) (3)))
```
Input pulses of width 1, 2 and 5 on a path with delay 4. Output: `Y 1 0`, `Y 57 1`, `Y 62 0`. The width-2 pulse produces no x (expected x around t35, then 0). That matches the default limits (= path delay), so the PATHPULSE values were not applied, and no warning was issued.

**Controls (pass in both editions):** IOPATH annotation replaces the source delay with rise 4 / fall 6 (`R1 0 R2 1 F1 1 F2 0`, p32_sdf.sv). The width-1 pulse is rejected and the width-5 pulse propagates, as expected under either limit set. The §30.7 default pulse rejection works for source-specified paths (Clause 30 probe).

**Expected:** with reject 2 and error 3, the width-2 pulse drives y to x (then back to 0) in both editions. If PATHPULSE is unsupported, at minimum the §32.3 warning is expected.

**Tool-mode note:** without -gspecify, $sdf_annotate is omitted with an explicit warning; that mode is not part of this issue.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'sdf_annotate', 'SDF', 'IOPATH', 'PATHPULSE', 'pulse limit', '32.' found no Clause 32 issue (evidence DEDUPE.md).
title: [IEEE 1800] §32.7 — SDF PATHPULSE limits are not applied (2-unit pulse with reject 2/error 3 is fully rejected; no annotation warning)

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §35.5.6.1 with Annex H (H.7.4, H.7.8); IEEE 1800-2023 same.

**Normative requirement:** imported subroutine formals may have unsized unpacked (open) dimensions. svDimensions/svSize etc. apply to any open array. Annex H.7.4 maps string elements to const char*, and H.7.8 defines the C layout for unpacked aggregates of non-scalar/non-packed elements.

**Probes** (current main cc25756d1, `-B` pinned, -g2017 and -g2023 identical):
- `string` open array (Slurm job 3566; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c35d-20261020/attempt-03-string-openarray/)
- unpacked-struct open array (Slurm job 3568; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c35d-20261020/attempt-04-struct-openarray/)

In both cases compilation returns 0 but prints:
`sorry: DPI import 'c_array_size': open array argument 'values' must have packed bit/logic or real elements; the call is skipped.`
At runtime the call is not made. It returns the default value, and the probe's `svSize` assertion fails. The C routine only queries svDimensions/svSize and does not access elements.

**Why this matters:** a legal call is silently dropped while compilation reports success. That is a semantic substitution, not just an unsupported diagnostic.

**Controls (pass):** open arrays of packed bit/logic and real elements (attempt-02-openarray-abi).

**Expected:** the import is called. svDimensions/svSize report the actual geometry, and the elements are accessible per Annex H, in both editions. If support were genuinely unavailable, the expected result is a compile error, not a skipped call with rc 0.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches on 'DPI open array' and 'svdpi bounds'. Closed #45 (broad open-array phase), #13, #505 (shortreal array imports), #506 (fixed-size unpacked export formals) and #544 (multidimensional fixed-array actuals) do not cover string or struct element open arrays.

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §20.12 with §16.3; IEEE 1800-2023 §20.11 with §16.3.

**Normative requirement:** $assertoff stops checking of the specified assertions until $asserton; $assertkill aborts them and stops checking until $asserton. §16.3 states that execution of simple immediate assertion action blocks is controlled by the assertion action control tasks.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c20/p20_12_ac1.sv and ac2.sv (Slurm job 3546, current main cc25756d1, `-B` pinned, -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c20d-20261020/attempt-02-isolate/remote-3546). Clock posedges every 10 time units from 5:
```systemverilog
a1: assert property (@(posedge clk) 1'b0) else cf++;          // concurrent
always @(posedge clk) a2: assert (1'b0) else imf++;            // simple immediate
$assertoff(0, a1, a2); #20 ... $asserton(0, a1, a2); #20 ... $assertkill(0, a1, a2); #20 ...
```
Observed (cf, imf): after off `0 2`, after on `2 4`, after kill `2 6`. The concurrent assertion is controlled correctly. The immediate assertion's else-action runs while off and after kill. With a no-argument `$assertoff;` (ac2) the immediate count is still `2` while off.

**Expected:** imf = 0 after the off window, 2 after the on window, and still 2 after kill, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches '$assertoff', '$asserton', '$assertkill', '$assertcontrol', 'assertion control', '20.12', '20.11'. Closed #444 (deferred-immediate pending-report cancellation) is related but distinct: it concerns deferred assertions' pending reports, not simple immediate assertions under the control tasks. The $assertcontrol absence is a separate issue.
title: [IEEE 1800] §20.12/§16.3 — $assertoff and $assertkill do not suppress simple immediate assertion failure actions

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §11.4.11; IEEE 1800-2023 §11.4.11. Same rule in both editions (exact text: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c11b-20261020/attempt-02-isolate/standard.md).

**Normative requirement:** the conditional operator can be used with aggregate expressions (operand types equivalent). When the condition is ambiguous, equal-length unpacked-array operands are combined element by element.

**Probes** (Slurm job 3541, current main cc25756d1, `-B` pinned, -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c11b-20261020/attempt-02-isolate/):
- q11_02_qa: `int A[3]='{1,2,3}, C[3]='{1,9,3}, D[3]; bit c; c = 1; D = c ? A : C;`
- q11_02_qx: `logic c = 1'bx; int A[2]='{1,5}, C[2]='{1,7}, D[2]; D = c ? A : C;`
- Both fail to compile: `sorry: a conditional with whole unpacked array operands is only supported when the condition is a constant.`

**Controls (pass in both editions):** a constant condition with array operands (`QK 2`); a runtime-condition conditional with unpacked-struct operands (`QS 3`); aggregate copy and ==/!= (`E 1 1 1 1`, `Y 2 7`); unequal-size array comparison rejected.

**Expected:** qa prints D[1] = 2. For qx, D[0] = 1, and D[1] is the bitwise merge of 5 and 7 (bit 1 = x), in both editions. The refusal is explicit rather than silent, but legal code cannot compile. The ambiguous-condition element merge is unassessable until this is fixed.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'sorry conditional', 'whole unpacked array operands', 'conditional aggregate', 'ternary unpacked', 'conditional struct', '11.4.11', plus 'aggregate equality', 'unpacked array ==', 'struct ==', '11.2.2', 'conditional unpacked'. Hits #728 (multidimensional array equality), #775 (let/cast) and #780 (assertion predicate) are unrelated.
title: [IEEE 1800] §11.4.11 — conditional operator with whole unpacked-array operands requires a constant condition (sorry)

**Normative requirement:** each item of an unpacked array concatenation has a self-determined type; a braced item whose operands form a vector (or string) concatenation is a self-determined vector (or string) concatenation and is a legal item. C = {{8'h01, 8'h02}, 3};   // inner item = 16'h0102 vector concatenation

**Normative requirement:** items of an unpacked array concatenation may be array-valued and freely mixed with element-valued items, provided each item's slowest-varying element is compatible with the target element type. The standard example `A9 = {A3, 4, 5, A3, 6};` (A3 a fixed-size array) is legal. (Excerpts: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c10d-20261020/attempt-01-uconcat/STANDARD.md.)

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §10.9.2 (pp.248–249); IEEE 1800-2023 §10.9.2 (pp.263–264).

**Normative requirement:** members not matched by a member-name key take the type or default key. A member that is itself an unpacked array (or structure) receives the type/default keys according to the array (or structure) pattern rules, so `default:` descends into its elements, and every member shall be covered. (Exact excerpts: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c10c-20261020/attempt-01-patterns/STANDARD.md.)

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c10/p10_09_struct_default_nested_array.sv (Slurm job 3528, current main cc25756d1, -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c10c-20261020/attempt-02-isolate-default/):
```systemverilog
typedef struct { int x; int y[2]; } T; T t;
t = '{default:5};        // expected x=5, y='{5,5}
t = '{x:1, default:6};   // expected x=1, y='{6,6}
```
Compile rc=2 with `error: integer literal is not compatible with an unpacked type in this context.` on both lines.

**Controls (pass in both editions):** direct `'{default:4}` on a 2-D unpacked array (`M 4 4 4 4`); explicit nested member patterns `'{x:0, y:'{default:5}}` (`C1 0 5 5`, `C2 1 6 6`); member-name > type-key > default precedence (`P3 7 1 9 1.0`); index keys, replication, positional patterns. The coverage, duplicate-index and element-count errors are enforced.

**Expected:** both assignments compile. They print `5 5 5` and `1 6 6`, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'assignment pattern', 'default:', 'pattern key', 'replication pattern', 'struct pattern default', '10.9' (evidence attempt-01-patterns/dedupe-results.md). #426 (open) covers expression keys and remaining key types, not default descent into aggregate members. #415 (nested array-return values), #474 (fixed-array parameters), #484/#485/#801 are unrelated.

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §20.7 (p.602); IEEE 1800-2023 §20.7. Reached via §7.11.

**Normative requirement:** "It shall be legal to call any of these query functions within a constant expression if all three of the following conditions are true: (1) the call would be legal in an expression, (2) the type operator … applied to the first argument would be legal and return some fixed-size type, and (3) any optional dimension expression is a constant expression." Standard example: `typedef logic [16:1] Word; Word Ram[0:9];`, where `$size(Ram,2)` returns 16.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c07/ q4b (Slurm job 3524, current main cc25756d1, -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c07f-20261020/attempt-02-split/):
```systemverilog
typedef logic [16:1] Word; Word Ram[0:9];
localparam int SR = $size(Ram, 2);
```
Compile error: `A reference to a net or variable (Ram) is not allowed in a constant expression.`

**Related but distinct:** #792 tracks wrong values for type-argument and runtime queries (`$size(Word)`; a runtime `$size(Ram,2)` prints x). This issue is the constant-expression legality rule: a fixed-size variable as the first argument must be accepted in constant contexts.

**Expected:** SR == 16 at elaboration, in both editions. Queries on fixed-size variables are usable in parameters, localparams and declaration ranges.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches recorded in evidence/ieee1800-audit-c07f-20261020/attempt-02-split/DEDUPE.md. #792/#793/#794 scopes reviewed; none tests the constant-expression form.
title: [IEEE 1800] §20.7 — array query on a fixed-size variable in a constant expression (localparam SR = $size(Ram,2)) is rejected

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2023 §7.12.4 (pp.177–178). This is 2023-only: 2017 §7.12.4 (p.169) has no optional index-name argument, so the -g2017 rejection is conforming.

**Normative requirement:** "By default, the index_method_name shall be index. However, this name may conflict with member variables or methods of items stored within the array. When this occurs, the optional index argument of the array method may be used to avoid the conflict." The standard example is `q = arr.find(item, iter_index) with (item.index != item.iter_index);`.

The 2023 §7.12.5 map() method, which also takes an iterator-name argument (`A.map(a) with (a + B[a.index])`), works, so the edition gate exists but the find-family path does not accept the second (index-name) argument.

**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §8.20 (p.184); IEEE 1800-2023 §8.20 (p.196). Same text in both editions.

**Normative requirement:** "Virtual method overrides in subclasses shall have matching argument types, identical argument names, identical qualifiers, and identical directions to the prototype." The return type shall be a matching type or a derived class type; "the presence of a default shall match."

**Probes** (evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c08o-20261020/attempt-02-const-override/, Slurm job 3502, current main cc25756d1, iverilog SHA256 1088dd26…). The base is `virtual function int f(int a)` (v5 base: `f(int a = 1)`). Each override compiles with rc=0 and no diagnostic in -g2017 and -g2023:
- v1 renamed argument `f(int b)`
- v2 changed argument type `f(byte a)`
- v3 changed direction `f(output int a)`
- v4 changed return type `function byte f(int a)`
- v5 default presence differs `f(int a)` versus base `f(int a = 1)`

**Controls (pass in both editions):** a covariant derived-class return type is accepted (V6), differing default expressions with matching presence are accepted (V7), and virtual-stays-virtual and polymorphic dispatch work. The related §8.24 out-of-block prototype mismatch is tracked separately as #847.

**Expected:** a compile-time error for each of v1–v5, in both editions. (In the 2023 Example 2, `E#()` with a non-matching argument type is labelled "Illegal".)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §8.21 (p.186); IEEE 1800-2023 §8.21.

**Normative requirement:** "Abstract classes may be extended to further abstract classes, but all pure virtual methods shall have overridden implementations in order to be extended by a non-abstract class."

**Probe:** evidence/ieee1800-audit-c08m-20261020/attempt-02-virtual/ and attempt-03-virtual/ (Slurm job 3498, current main cc25756d1, iverilog SHA256 1088dd26…, -g2017 and -g2023 identical):
```systemverilog
virtual class AbstractBase; pure virtual function integer send(); endclass
class MissingImplementation extends AbstractBase; endclass
```
- Compiles with no diagnostic. An object is constructed, and calling `send()` executes and prints `MISSING x`.

**Controls (pass in both editions):**
- §8.21 errors are enforced for direct construction of an abstract class, a pure method in a non-virtual class, and a pure method with a body.
- The analogous obligations elsewhere are enforced: a non-abstract class missing an interface-class method (§8.26) and a non-abstract class missing a pure constraint (§18.5.2) are both compile errors.
- Positive §§8.20–8.22: virtual stays virtual (`C C`), virtual overriding non-virtual (`A2 C2`), abstract constructor chaining (`5`), a body-less method returns x, polymorphic array dispatch (`Ether Token GPS`).

**Expected:** a compile-time error when a non-virtual (non-abstract) class extends an abstract class without overriding every inherited pure virtual method, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'virtual method', 'abstract class', 'abstract', 'pure virtual', 'polymorphism', '8.20', '8.21', 'unimplemented pure', 'pure method', 'missing pure', 'virtual class', 'abstract method', 'virtual base', 'pure method implementation', 'instantiate abstract', 'missing implementation' matched only unrelated #455, #845, #609, #615, #766, #642, #842, #650, #30, #9, #27.

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §8.26 (p.194). Edition-specific: IEEE 1800-2023 §8.26 (p.206) narrows the rule.

**Normative requirement (2017):** “An interface class shall not be nested within another class.”

**2023 (changed):** “An interface class shall not be nested within another interface class.” Nesting inside an ordinary class is therefore legal in 2023.

**Probe:** `tests/1800_audit/c08/neg/n08_26_nested_interface.sv` (evidence: `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c08k-20261020/attempt-01-iface/`, Slurm job 3492, main `cc25756d1`):

```systemverilog
class Outer;
  interface class Nested;
    pure virtual function void f();
  endclass
endclass
```

- `-g2017`: compile rc=0, no diagnostic. This is the gap.
- `-g2023`: compile rc=0. This is conforming.

**Expected:** Under `-g2017` (and earlier editions), reject an interface class declared inside any class. Under `-g2023`, keep accepting it. In both editions, an interface class nested inside another interface class must be rejected because nested classes are prohibited in an interface class.

**Controls:** The standard Fifo/Stack example, `extends` inheritance, missing-implementation rejection, constraint-in-interface-class rejection, and non-pure-method rejection all conform in both editions.

**Dedupe:** Open-and-closed searches for `interface class`, `implements`, `8.26`, `pure virtual interface class`, `nested interface class`, and `interface class inside class` found no matching issue. #5, #27, #30, #434, #533, and #841 were inspected and are unrelated.
title: [IEEE 1800-2017] §8.26 — -g2017 accepts an interface class nested within a class (2017-only restriction; legal in 2023)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.12 (p.521); IEEE 1800-2023 §18.5.11.

**Normative requirement:** "Functions shall be called before constraints are solved, and their return values shall be treated as state variables." … "Random variables used as function arguments shall establish an implicit variable ordering or priority." So v is solved first, then length is solved against the constraints that reference it.

**Probes** (Slurm jobs 3488/3489, current main cc25756d1, -g2017 and -g2023 identical; evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18p-20261020/attempt-01-func/ and attempt-02-f2diag/):
```systemverilog
function automatic int count_ones(bit [9:0] w); ... endfunction  // standard example
class F2; rand bit [9:0] v; rand bit [3:0] length;
  constraint c1 { length == count_ones(v); length < 3; } endclass
```
- F2: 0/200 successful randomize() calls. Under the standard's ordering a call succeeds when popcount(v) < 3, p = 56/1024 ≈ 0.055, so about 11/200 is expected; P(0) ≈ 1.3e-5.
- F4, the same constraints in two separate blocks: 0/200.
- D3: 0/20. Values are left unchanged after each failure (v=3, len=2 from the preceding call).
- No warning or error is printed, only rc=0.

**Controls (pass):**
- F1 `length == count_ones(v)` alone: 200/200 correct.
- D0: v drawn from F1 is uniform (count_ones(v)<3 in 21/400 versus about 22 expected).
- D1 `with { v == 10'b11; }`: rc=1, len=2.
- D2 `with { v == 10'h3FF; }`: rc=0, which is correct.
- const ref function argument: OK. output/ref arguments are rejected as required.

**Expected:** with v solved first (uniformly) and length then solved as length == count_ones(v) under length < 3, about 5.5% of calls succeed, each with length == count_ones(v) < 3. A bidirectional solve that always succeeds would also be conforming in effect, but never succeeding is not. The failing calls also give no diagnostic.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'function in constraint', 'constraint function call', '18.5.12', 'function implicit ordering', plus six searches on function-result state/ordering/joint randomization, returned only closed #680 (non-rand function args in inline constraints) and #494 (queue-size leaves). Neither covers this.
title: [IEEE 1800] §18.5.12 (2023 §18.5.11) — constraining a function result variable further (length == f(v); length < 3) makes randomize() always fail

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.10 (p.518); IEEE 1800-2023 §18.5.9. Context: 2017 §18.5.9 / 2023 §18.5.8 global constraints.

**Normative requirement:** "The solver shall assure that the random values are selected to give a uniform value distribution over legal value combinations (that is, all combinations of legal values have the same probability of being the solution)."

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_9_g1.sv, the standard's Figure 18-2 heap example (`class A; rand bit [7:0] v; endclass`, `class B extends A; rand A left, right; constraint heapcond {left.v <= v; right.v > v;} endclass`). Evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18o-20261020/attempt-02-split/ (Slurm job 3486, current main cc25756d1, -g2017 and -g2023).
- All 20 calls succeed and satisfy the constraint (bad=0).
- Every run warns: `Warning: a joint randomization component is too large to enumerate exactly; it is sampled against the hard constraints, not uniformly over its solutions (further similar warnings suppressed).`
- The unsplit run of 200 calls exceeded 30 s.
- Control: the same structure with 4-bit v (p18_05_9_g1s.sv, 4096 combinations) gives no warning and is correct (bad=0, left_lt=165/200).

**Observed gap:** the implementation itself states that, for a component of this size (three 8-bit variables, about 16.7M combinations), the solution is not drawn uniformly over the legal combinations. A warning does not make the non-uniform distribution conforming.

**Expected:** every legal (left.v, v, right.v) combination equally probable, regardless of component size, using an exact-uniform method such as counting-based or hash-based uniform sampling over the satisfying set. No 'not uniformly' fallback. Satisfiability and global-constraint semantics already conform (G1/G2/G3 bad=0).

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'too large to enumerate', 'not uniformly over its solutions', 'uniform value distribution joint', 'uniform value distribution', 'uniform over legal value combinations', 'joint randomization', 'sampled against the hard constraints', 'uniform constraint solver' returned no issue. #478/#491/#832/#840 were reviewed and are unrelated.
title: [IEEE 1800] §18.5.10 (2023 §18.5.9) — large joint randomization components are sampled non-uniformly (standard 8-bit heap example)

**Expected:** a compile-time error for each case, in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'extern constraint', 'constraint prototype', 'pure constraint', 'constraint inheritance', 'external constraint block', 'constraint override', 'constraint prototype same name block', '18.5.1', '18.5.2' found no matching issue. #841 (module-scope external blocks rejected) is a different gap.
