body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2023 §18.4 (rand real permitted), §11.4.13 (p.288, set membership), §18.5.3 (p.532). 2017 is N/A because 2017 §18.4 does not allow rand real, and -g2017 correctly rejects the declaration.

**Normative requirement:** §11.4.13: "SystemVerilog supports singular value sets and a set membership operator." §18.5.3: "The distribution set is a comma-separated list of integral or real expressions and ranges." A rand real constrained to a set of discrete real values is a satisfiable constraint.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_4_unique_real_scalar.sv (evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18k-20261020/attempt-03-real-controls/, Slurm job 3458, current main cc25756d1, -g2023), 100 randomize() calls per class:
- C0 `rand real r; constraint c { r inside {1.0, 2.0, 3.0}; }`: ok=0
- C3 `rand real r1, r2; r1 inside {1.0, 2.0}; r2 inside {1.0, 2.0}; r1 != r2;`: ok=0
- R1 (three reals in {1.0,2.0,3.0} with unique): ok=0
- Every call reports `ERROR: global constraint sampling failed: no feasible binary64 value satisfies the finite real interval.` (301 occurrences).
- Controls pass: C1 `r >= 1.0; r <= 3.0;` ok=100 bad=0; C2 interval-bounded `unique {r1, r2}` ok=100 bad=0. Real unique and real interval bounds work; only the value-set form fails.

**Expected:** randomize() succeeds and r takes one of 1.0, 2.0, 3.0 (C0). C3 yields {r1,r2} = {1.0,2.0} in some order. R1 yields a permutation of 1.0, 2.0, 3.0.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'real inside', 'binary64 feasible', 'finite real interval', 'rand real constraint', 'unique real' found only open #463. #463 tracks rand-real shapes beyond scalar finite intervals (arrays/aggregates, distribution) but does not name inside value sets on a scalar rand real. This issue is the narrower scalar value-set gap; cross-reference #463.
title: [IEEE 1800-2023] §18.4/§11.4.13 — rand real constrained by an inside value set ({1.0, 2.0, 3.0}) is always infeasible

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.5 (pp.513–514); IEEE 1800-2023 §18.5.4 (p.534).

**Normative requirement:** each item in the uniqueness group "shall be … An unpacked array variable whose leaf element type is integral [2023: or real], or a slice of such a variable". The standard's own example is `unique {b, a[2:3], excluded};`.

**Probes** (Slurm jobs 3441/3442/3456, current main cc25756d1, -g2017 and -g2023, identical results):
- tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_5_unique.sv, U1 (the standard example verbatim): `U1 rc_ok=0 bad=500`, so all 500 randomize() calls fail.
- tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_5_unique_shapes.sv (each class has `rand byte a[5], b, e;`, 50 calls each):
  - S1 `unique {a[2:3]}`: ok=0
  - S4 `unique {b, a[2:3]}`: ok=0
  - S5 `unique {b, a[2:3], e}`: ok=0
  - Controls pass with ok=50 bad=0: S2 `unique {b, e}`, S3 `unique {b, a}` (whole array), S6 `unique {a[1], a[3]}` (constant-index elements).
- Compile warning: `Constraint item in 'u' of class U1 is not representable in the constraint solver; randomize() of this class will fail.`
- Runtime: `ERROR: constraint state read: the constraint item at …:4 is not supported by the constraint solver; randomize() fails rather than ignore it.`
- The refusal is explicit, not a silent drop, but legal code cannot be randomized.

Evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18k-20261020/attempt-01-unique/ (including remote-results-3456/).

**Expected:** a slice `a[l:r]` in a uniqueness group contributes its elements as members. The standard example randomizes successfully with b, a[2], a[3] and excluded pairwise distinct and none of b, a[2], a[3] equal to 5.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'unique constraint', 'uniqueness', '18.5.5', 'unique slice', 'unique array constraint', 'unique variables', 'unique', 'constraint state read not supported' found no matching issue. #838 (illegal-member diagnostics) is a different gap.
title: [IEEE 1800] §18.5.5 (2023 §18.5.4) — unique constraint with an array-slice member is refused by the solver (randomize() always fails)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.5 (pp.513–514); IEEE 1800-2023 §18.5.4 (p.534). Both rules are present in both editions.

**Normative requirements:**
1. "All members of the group of variables so specified … shall be of equivalent type."
2. Footnote to Syntax 18-4: the open_range_list (2023: range_list) "shall contain only expressions that denote scalar [2023: singular] or array variables".

**Probes** (evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18k-20261020/attempt-01-unique/, Slurm job 3441, current main cc25756d1):
- tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_5_n2_type.sv: `class C; rand byte x; rand int y; constraint c { unique {x, y}; } endclass`. byte and int are not equivalent types (§6.22.2: different widths).
- tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_5_n3_expr.sv: `class C; rand byte x, y; constraint c { unique {x + 1, y}; } endclass`
- Both are instantiated with `C o = new;`. Observed in -g2017 and -g2023: compile rc=0, run rc=0, no diagnostic.

**Control:** the sibling restriction is enforced. A randc member fails with `'randc' variables cannot be used in 'unique' constraints.` in both editions. Legal groups work: whole-array permutation (24/24 permutations), pigeonhole unsatisfiable (rc=0), one-member group has no effect, sized dynamic-array permutation.

**Expected:** a compile-time (elaboration) error for each of: (1) group members whose types are not equivalent; (2) a group item that is not a variable reference (for example an operator expression such as `x + 1`). This applies in both editions.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'unique constraint', 'uniqueness', '18.5.5', 'unique randc', 'unique equivalent type', 'unique slice', 'unique array constraint', 'unique variables', 'unique expression constraint', 'unique' matched only unrelated #19, #11, #27 (closed) and #778 (case defaults).
title: [IEEE 1800] §18.5.5 (2023 §18.5.4) — illegal uniqueness-group members accepted silently (non-equivalent types, non-variable expressions)

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.4 (pp.512–513) versus IEEE 1800-2023 §18.5.3 (pp.532–533). The editions differ; this is a -g2017 conformance gap.

**Normative requirement (2017):** "The := operator assigns the specified weight to the item or, if the item is a range, to every value in the range." (2017 example: with `x != 200`, the excluded value's weight is removed and the ratio becomes 1-5.)
**2023 (changed):** range_weight = range_size × specified_weight, "including values which may be excluded from the solution space based on other constraints"; the example `x > 101; x dist {[100:102]:=1, 103:=1};` gives 3:1.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_3_dist2023.sv, class E3: `rand int x; constraint c { x > 101; x dist {[100:102] := 1, 103 := 1}; }`, 8000 randomizations. Evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18j-20261020/attempt-01-dist2023/ (Slurm job 3437, current main cc25756d1).
- -g2023: `102:6070 103:1930`, which conforms (3:1).
- -g2017: `102:6070 103:1930`, which does not conform. 2017 per-value weighting gives 102 and 103 weight 1 each, so the result should be about 4000:4000 (±5σ ≈ ±225).

**Expected:** under -g2017 (and earlier editions), := on a range gives each value the item weight, and values excluded by other constraints contribute nothing (102:103 ≈ 1:1). Under -g2023, keep the current whole-range behaviour. The same edition split applies to :/ ranges with excluded values: 2017 gives each value range_weight/n, while 2023 keeps the whole range weight.

**Dedupe:** open+closed searches 'dist additive weight', 'dist range weight excluded', '18.5.3', 'soft dist', 'dist in:title', 'distribution constraint' found only #836 (no-rand rule), closed #8/#12 (general dist support, no edition semantics) and #463 (real ranges). None covers this.
title: [IEEE 1800] §18.5.4 — -g2017 applies the 2023 whole-range dist weight when range values are excluded by other constraints

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.4 (p.513); IEEE 1800-2023 §18.5.3 (p.533). Same rule in both editions.

**Normative requirement:** "Limitations are as follows: … A dist expression requires that the expression contain at least one rand variable."

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_4_n2_norand.sv, evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18i-20261020/attempt-02-dist-case-split/ (Slurm job 3436, current main cc25756d1).

```systemverilog
class C; int s; constraint c { s dist {1 := 1, 2 := 1}; } endclass
```
instantiated with `C o = new;`. Observed in -g2017 and -g2023: compile rc=0, no diagnostic.

Control: the sibling limitation is enforced. `randc bit [3:0] x; constraint c { x dist {...}; }` fails with `error: 'randc' variables cannot be used in 'dist' constraints.` in both editions. Positive dist semantics (:= / :/ weights, zero weight as constraint, runtime weight expressions, hard membership) all pass in the same probe set.

title: [IEEE 1800] §18.5.4 (2023 §18.5.3) — dist expression with no rand variable is accepted silently

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §19.7 (pp.578–579); IEEE 1800-2023 §19.7 (pp.605–606).

**Normative requirement:** "Each instance of a covergroup can initialize an instance-specific option to a different value." … "Option assignment statements in the covergroup definition are evaluated at the time that the covergroup is instantiated." Table 19-1 lists at_least and auto_bin_max as instance-specific options.

**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c19/p19_07_option_args.sv (evidence: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c19b-20261020/attempt-02-option-args/). Current main cc25756d1, -g2017 and -g2023, identical results.
- `option.at_least = al;` (covergroup argument), `option.auto_bin_max = abm;` at covergroup level and at coverpoint level.
- Compile: `sorry: covergroup option 'at_least' is not a constant; using default 1.` and twice `sorry: covergroup option 'auto_bin_max' is not a constant; using default 64.`
- Run: `ATL_ARG2 100.00 ATL_LIT2 0.00` (at_least=3 from argument ignored; literal 3 works); `ABM_CG_ARG 1.56 ABM_CP_ARG 1.56 ABM_LIT 25.00` (auto_bin_max=4 from argument ignored, 64 bins used; literal 4 works).
- Control: `option.weight = w;` from a constructor argument is honoured (type coverage 87.50 for weights 3:1 in p19_11_3_type_cov.sv).

**Expected:** each option RHS is evaluated at instantiation with the instance's constructor arguments: ATL_ARG2 0.00, ATL_ARG3 100.00, ABM_CG_ARG 25.00, ABM_CP_ARG 25.00, with no sorry. This also blocks §19.11.1 (cumulative coverage uses the maximum at_least across instances) and §19.11.3 merged bin naming across instances with different auto_bin_max.

**Dedupe:** distinct from #689 (post-construction procedural option assignment; it does not cover definition-time non-constant RHS). Search '"not a constant" covergroup' returned no issues; at_least/auto_bin_max searches hit only #689, #687, #696 (unrelated).
title: [IEEE 1800] §19.7 — non-constant covergroup option assignments (at_least, auto_bin_max) fall back to the default instead of the per-instance value

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §18.5.10 p.520 / 2023 §18.5.9.
**Normative:** "The following restrictions apply to variable ordering: Only random variables are allowed, that is, they shall be rand. ... There shall be no circular dependencies in the ordering, such as solve a before b combined with solve b before a."
**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c18/neg_n18_solve_nonrand.sv (`class C; int a; rand int b; constraint o { solve a before b; } endclass`, instantiated and randomized) and neg_n18_solve_circular.sv (`solve a before b; solve b before a;`, instantiated and randomized).
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023, current main cc25756d): the non-random target compiles and randomizes (rc=0) with no diagnostic. The circular ordering compiles with a warning that the ordering directive is ignored, and randomize() returns 1. The ordering semantics themselves pass (the standard Table 18-1/18-2 example gives s==1 0/400 unordered and 197/400 ordered), and a randc target is correctly rejected.
**Expected:** a compile-time error for a non-random ordering target and for a circular ordering. Low priority diagnostic gap; decide with the user whether the circular case must be an error rather than a warning, since the standard states the restriction without naming the tool response.

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §18.5.11 p.521 / 2023 §18.5.10.
**Normative:** "If a constraint block is declared as static, then calls to constraint_mode() shall affect all instances of the specified constraint in all objects. Thus, if a static constraint is set to OFF, it is off for all instances of that particular class."
**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c18/p18_05_order_static.sv and the reducers in evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18f-20261020/attempt-02-reducers/ (`class S; rand int x; static constraint c { x == 5; } endclass`, two instances a and b).

Re-enabling through b leaves a at mode 0, and `a.randomize() with { x == 7; }` returns 1. The static constraint is still enforced while enabled, and a mismatched static qualifier between prototype and external block is correctly rejected.

**Normative (the standard example):** `event done, blast; event done_too = done; task trigger( event ev ); -> ev; endtask ... fork @ done_too; #1 trigger( done ); join` "shows ... how an event can be passed to a generic task that triggers the event."

**Clause:** 2017 §6.7.1 p.98 and §23.2.2.3 p.703 / 2023 §6.7.1, §23.2.2.3.
**Normative:** "A valid data type for a net shall be one of the following: a) A 4-state integral type, including a packed array or packed structure. b) A fixed-size unpacked array or unpacked structure, where each element has a valid data type for a net." For an input port with the kind omitted, "the port shall default to a net of default net type".
**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c26/r26_vp_f.sv (`module M (input bit [7:0] a); endmodule`), and r26_hdr_a.sv, r26_hdr_b.sv, r26_hdr_d.sv (an input port whose type is a package typedef of bit [7:0]); r26_st_g.sv (an input port of a packed struct with a bit member).

**Expected:** a compile error for a net whose data type is two-state (the legal spellings are `input var bit [7:0] a` or a 4-state type). Low priority diagnostic gap; existing code may rely on the permissive behavior, so decide the enforcement policy with the user. The standard own example in section 26.4 uses a struct of bit members as an input port type and conflicts with this rule as written, so the example is not used as evidence.

**Clause:** 2017 §23.2.2.3 p.705 / 2023 §23.2.2.3.
**Normative:** ANSI port declarations may be explicitly named: `ansi_port_declaration ::= ... | [ port_direction ] . port_identifier ( [ expression ] )`, and "A port declaration that immediately follows an explicit port declaration shall inherit only the port direction (if not explicitly specified) from the explicit port declaration". The standard example: `module mh22 (input wire integer p_a, .p_b(s_b), p_c); logic [5:0] s_b;` where p_b inherits the input direction, and p_c inherits only the direction from p_b and defaults to the net port kind and the logic data type.
**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c23/p23_02b_mh22_probe.sv (the standard example verbatim).
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023): compile error "Superfluous comma in port declaration list." at the header.
**Expected:** the header is accepted; p_a is an input wire integer, p_b is an explicitly named input port whose type is that of s_b, and p_c is an input wire logic. Not a gap (probe errors withdrawn): the mh3 header with no direction is an inout port, so connecting a literal to it is correctly rejected, and an output port with an explicit data type is a variable, so an initializer on it is legal.

body:
## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module display_width;
  initial begin
    $display("%02X", 32'h3);
    $finish;
  end
endmodule
```

## Expected vs observed

The Caliptra row 93/97 command reader expects the one-byte opcode text `03`. On the exact M20 Icarus pin (`cae035642e056644274a01e98d4422ce286685b4`, Icarus 13.0 devel), the reproducer prints `00000003`; when the reader consumes the first byte pair from an eight-digit command such as `00000001`, it sees opcode `00` and dispatches key generation.

IEEE 1800-2017 §21.2.1.3 says a field wider than its specified width expands to contain the converted value, without truncation. Thus the observed `00000003` is the standard-defined output for this 32-bit expression. The Caliptra expectation is an application compatibility mismatch, not an Icarus conformance claim.

The M20 run-local overlay explicitly sizes the command expression to the opcode width and restored rows 93/97. This issue records the exact-pin behavior and asks whether a compatibility note or other guidance is useful for similar callers.
title: from-caliptra-dv: %02X expands a 32-bit command beyond the expected opcode width

**Normative:** `cond_predicate ::= expression_or_cond_pattern { &&& expression_or_cond_pattern }`; "The predicate in an if–else statement can be a series of clauses separated with the &&& operator." §12.6.3 allows the same predicate in a conditional expression (e1 ? e2 : e3). The standard's Example 2: `if (e matches (tagged Jmp .j) &&& j matches (tagged JmpC '{cc:c,addr:a}))`.
**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c12/r12_06_g2.sv (`if (y &&& (y>0)) hit=1; else hit=2;`), r12_06_g3.sv (`if (y &&& z) ...`), r12_06_g5.sv and r12_06_f7.sv (`if (v matches tagged Valid .n &&& (n==5)) ...`, with and without parentheses on the guard); conditional operator: r12_06_h3.sv (`nv = v matches tagged Valid .n &&& n>3 ? n : -1;`), h4 (`... n>7 ...`), h5 (`nv = y &&& (y>0) ? 1 : 2;`), h6 (`nv = y &&& z ? 1 : 2;`); control r12_06_g1.sv (`if (v matches tagged Valid .n) hit=n;`).
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023): a `&&&` clause in the predicate of an if statement or of the conditional operator fails to compile (syntax error / malformed statement), for plain expression clauses and for pattern clauses. `if (v matches tagged Valid .n &&& (n==5))` also aborts the compiler (assertion in pform_finish_procedural_block, Abort trap). The unguarded `if` form passes (`g1 hit=5`).
**Expected:** all clauses are evaluated left to right and all must succeed; with v = tagged Valid(5): g2 gives 1, g3 gives 2, g5 gives 20, h3 gives 5, h4 gives -1, h5 gives 1, h6 gives 2. Related, not covering: #779 (the same operator on a pattern case item).

The shared sentence is: “It shall not be a bit-select or a part-select of a variable.” Bit-selects and part-selects of vector nets remain legal for force and release.
**Probes:** `tests/1800_audit/c10/neg/n10_06_assign_bitsel.sv` (`logic [3:0] q; initial assign q[0] = 1;`) and `tests/1800_audit/c10/neg/n10_06_force_var_bitsel.sv` (`logic [3:0] q; initial force q[1] = 1;`).

**Expected:** a compile error for each. A constant bit-select or part-select of a vector net stays legal for force and release and must not break. Closed #493 (release of selected packed subfields) is related but distinct: it is not about this restriction on variable targets. Low-priority diagnostic gap; do not enforce without user approval.

body:
**Clause:** IEEE 1800-2017 §10.6 p.242 / IEEE 1800-2023 §10.6.
**Normative:** “If any variable on the right-hand side of the assignment changes, the assignment shall be reevaluated while the assign or force is in effect.”
**Probe:** `tests/1800_audit/c10/p10_06b_force_release.sv` is the standard's Example 2; reductions are `r10_06a_multi_rhs_update.sv` and `r10_06a_multi_rhs_staged.sv`, with single-variable controls `r10_06a_assign_rhs_update.sv` and `r10_06a_force_release_assign.sv` in the same directory.
**Observed:** in both `-g2017` and `-g2023`, the standard example prints `0 d=x,e=0`, `10 d=1,e=1`, `20 d=x,e=0` where the standard shows `0 d=0,e=0`, `10 d=1,e=1`, `20 d=0,e=0`. Compilation warns that the procedural continuous assignment RHS is evaluated only once. The reduced `assign d = a & b & c` ends at `d=x` after `a=1, b=0, c=1`, both with simultaneous and staged changes. A single-variable RHS and single-variable assign/force/release control pass. A changing multi-operand RHS under `force` was not isolated.

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §6.10 p.103 and §6.21 p.126 / 2023 §6.10 and §6.21 p.133.
**Normative:** "In the absence of an explicit declaration, an implicit net of default net type shall be assumed in the following circumstances" (a port expression declaration, a port-connection or primitive-terminal list, the left side of a continuous assignment). §6.21: "A variable declaration shall precede any simple reference (non-hierarchical) to that variable."
**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c06/r06_10_gen_ctrl_b.sv (plain undeclared name) and r06_10_gen_ctrl_a.sv (the same name implied inside a generate block and referenced outside it).
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023): `module m; initial begin $display("S"); $display(w2); $display("E"); end endmodule` compiles with only "Unable to bind ... w2" as a warning and runs, printing `S`, a blank line and `E`. The undeclared name evaluates to nothing and the statement still executes. The generate-scope case behaves identically, so the §6.10 generate-scope scoping rule cannot be tested while this is accepted. Existing records: docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md lines 2561-2566 (Slang rejects it as "use of undeclared identifier") and BLOCKERS.md line 4091 (the same warning in application runs).
**Expected:** a compile error for a reference to an undeclared identifier outside the implicit-net circumstances. The behavior substitutes a blank value for a requested one, which the project's no-fallback policy prohibits. Enforcement turns currently passing compiles that hide real unresolved names into hard failures, so decide the policy with the user before changing it.

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §6.22.1(e),(f) p.129 / 2023 §6.22.1(e),(f).
**Normative (the standard's own examples):** `typedef bit signed [7:0] BYTE; // matches the byte type`, `typedef bit signed [0:7] ETYB; // does not match the byte type`, and `typedef logic [1:0][3:0] NIBBLES; typedef logic [7:0] MY_BYTE; // MY_BYTE and NIBBLES are not matching types`.
**Probes:** tests/1800_audit/c06/p06_23b_type_scalar.sv (FAIL range_direction); tests/1800_audit/c06/p06_23g_array_mismatch.sv (prints MATCH=1).
**Observed:** both wrong results, with no diagnostic:
- `type(ETYB) != type(byte)` evaluates false: the range direction [0:7] versus [7:0] is ignored.
- `type(NIBBLES) != type(MY_BYTE)` evaluates false (the probe prints MATCH=1): packed dimensionality is ignored.
The other scalar checks pass (same type, typedef aliases, `type(BYTE) == type(byte)`, `type(int) == type(bit signed [31:0])`, builtin types distinct).
**Expected:** `type(ETYB) != type(byte)` and `type(NIBBLES) != type(MY_BYTE)` are both true. Packed-vector type matching must account for range direction and packed dimensions, not only width, state and signing. Related: #756 (struct, union and unpacked-array comparisons rejected).

The cases are the spec's own examples: two anonymous structs declared together versus a separately declared one, two typedef structs, and the matching unpacked arrays `MEM_BYTES`/`MY_MEM_BYTES`.
**Expected:** `type(an1) == type(an2)`, `type(an1) != type(an3)`, `type(ab1) == type(ab2)`, `type(ab3) != type(ab1)`, `type(MEM_BYTES) == type(MY_MEM_BYTES)`.

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §6.24.2 p.134 / 2023 §6.24.2 p.141 (the two editions differ).
**Normative:** 2017: "No type checking is done by the compiler, except to check that the destination variable and source expression are singulars." 2023: "The assignment is invalid if the arguments are singular and not cast compatible or the arguments are not singular and not assignment compatible."
**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c06/p06_24f_nonsingular.sv.
**Observed** (same under -g2017 and -g2023): `int arr[2]; arr = '{7,8}; r = $cast(arr, 1);` compiles, returns r=1 and leaves arr unchanged (7,8). A following task-form `$cast(arr, 1)` runs silently with arr unchanged and rc=0.
**Expected:**
- 2017: a compile-time error for the non-singular argument.
- 2023: the code compiles; the function form returns 0 (the assignment is invalid) with arr unchanged and no error; the task form issues a run-time error with arr unchanged.
In both editions, returning 1 without assigning is wrong. The task-form error is the same missing-diagnostic class as the issue for invalid enum task casts.

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §6.24.2 p.134 / 2023 §6.24.2 p.141.
**Normative:** "When called as a task, `$cast` attempts to assign the source expression to the destination variable. If the assignment is invalid, a run-time error occurs, and the destination variable is left unchanged."
**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c06/p06_24e_task_invalid.sv.
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023): `typedef enum {red,green,blue,yellow} Colors; Colors col = green; $cast(col, 10); $cast(col, -1);` leave col unchanged (1) but print no run-time error; the following valid `$cast(col, 2)` works (col=2) and the run reaches the end with rc=0.
**Expected:** each invalid task-form call reports a run-time error and leaves the destination unchanged. Wording and whether the run continues are implementation-defined; a silent invalid call is not conformant. The function form (returns 0, no error) is correct and passes 10/10 in tests/1800_audit/c06/p06_24b_dyn_cast.sv.

body:
**Clause:** 2017 §6.24.2 p.134 / 2023 §6.24.2 p.141.
**Normative:** 2017: "When called as a function, `$cast` attempts to assign the source expression to the destination variable and returns 1 if the cast is legal." 2023: "...returns 1 if the assignment is valid. If the assignment is invalid, the function does not make the assignment and returns 0."
**Probe:** `tests/1800_audit/c06/r06_24b_real_cast_isolate.sv`.
**Observed** (identical under -g2017 and -g2023): `$cast(int_dest, 3.7)` returns 1 with int_dest=4, then `$cast(real_dest, 7)` prints "sorry: Format 9 not implemented for putting real values." and "Assertion failed: (0), function real_from_vpi_value, file vpi_priv.cc, line 1067." and exits 250. Control: the plain assignment `real rv; rv = 7;` prints rv=7.000000 in both editions.
**Expected:** `$cast(rv, 7)` returns 1, rv == 7.0, with no abort. An integer-to-real assignment is a valid assignment. Related forms (real source into a real destination, the task form, shortreal) were not probed.

**Clause:** 2017 §6.19.5.3/§6.19.5.6/§6.19.5.7 (pp.118-119) and §6.16.1 / 2023 §6.19.5.3/§6.19.5.6/§6.19.5.7 (pp.123-124) and §6.16.1.
**Normative:** name() "returns the string representation of the given enumeration value"; str.len() "returns the length of the string, i.e., the number of characters in the string."
**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c06/r06_19l_lenbare.sv, r06_19l_nextname.sv (plus r06_19l_len.sv, r06_19l_upper.sv).
**Observed** (typedef enum {red,green,blue} Colors; Colors c = green):
- c.name.len compiles with "Method name nesting on enum not fully supported (compile-progress fallback)" and evaluates to 1 (expected 5 if accepted).
- c.next.name compiles with the same warning and prints a control character (expected "blue" if accepted).
- c.name.len() and c.name.toupper() fail to compile: Object t.c has no method "name.len(...)".
- Explicit forms work: c.name().len() = 5, c.next().name() = blue. A plain string control, s.len, s.toupper(), works.
**Expected:** each construct is either evaluated correctly or rejected with an error. A warning that substitutes a wrong value is not acceptable. Whether a method call on a paren-less enum method result is legal is not decided here; it is being checked with a differential run and will be added in a comment. Related but not covering: #739 (bare methods on a class property, "expression dropped"), #43.

**Clause:** 2017 §6.16.12–6.16.14 / 2023 §6.16.12–6.16.14.
**Normative:** "str.hextoa(i) stores the ASCII hexadecimal representation of i into str (inverse of atohex)." octtoa/bintoa are the same for octal/binary; atohex/atooct/atobin do not parse a sign.
**Probe:** tests/1800_audit/c06/r06_16_diag_D.sv, p06_16d_conv.sv (FAIL hex_rt).
**Observed:** hextoa(255)=ff and hextoa(32'h7fffffff)=7fffffff are correct. hextoa(-1)='-1'; hextoa(32'h80000000)='-80000000'; hextoa(32'hdeadbeef)='-21524111'; octtoa(-1)='-1'; octtoa(32'o20000000000)='-20000000000'; bintoa(-1)='-1'; bintoa(32'h80000000)='-1' followed by 31 zeros. itoa(32'h80000000)='-2147483648' is correct (decimal of a signed integer).
**Expected:** bit-pattern digits with no sign (ffffffff, 80000000, deadbeef, 37777777777, 20000000000, 32 ones) so that atohex(hextoa(i)) == i.

Provenance: build b9441baf (descendant of origin/main 8c95b5cc); cases C/D also reproduced on fafa4995 (in origin/main). Identical under -g2017 and -g2023. Probes: branch m7-1800-audit-c08, tests/1800_audit/c06/. Raw logs: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c06a-20261019/diag2/. Dedupe: open and closed issue searches for len, hextoa, octtoa, bintoa, string member, string struct, index class property, assertion array_size, string byte assignment, and implicit string found no exact gap matches. Reviewed related #100, #429, #484, and #503; their scopes do not cover these findings. Raw searches: evidence/ieee1800-audit-c06a-20261019/dedupe2/.
title: [IEEE 1800] §6.16.12-.14 — hextoa/octtoa/bintoa print a signed magnitude for values with bit 31 set

### Standard clause
- IEEE 1800-2017 §7.4.3 (array operations)
- IEEE 1800-2023 §7.4.6 (array operations)

### Normative requirement
Both clauses permit equality operations on arrays, packed or unpacked, with equivalent operand types.

### Probe and observed result
Probe: `tests/1800_audit/c07/p07_04_multidimensional_array_equality.sv`, Slurm job 3225, using Icarus main `c31cbf1b` under both `-g2017` and `-g2023`. The standard-valid 2D unpacked-array comparisons `left != right` and `left == right` fail compilation in each edition with exit 4:

```text
error: Array left needs an array index here.
error: Array right needs an array index here.
error: Array left needs an array index here.
error: Array right needs an array index here.
```

A one-dimensional unpacked-array equality/inequality control compiles and runs in both editions. This is distinct from closed issue #538, which covers VVP flag exhaustion on a large one-dimensional array.

Evidence: `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c07-20261019/attempt-05-c07-multidimensional-array-equality-corrected/README.md` and `results-3225.tar.gz` (SHA-256 `e066507c8aa7f36ef6569af9e8911272c50f78f3f6c9ab6b49c339a104b525ec`).

### Expected behavior
Equality and inequality must operate on compatible unpacked arrays across all dimensions in both language editions.
title: [IEEE 1800] §7.4.3/7.4.6 — Support equality and inequality on multidimensional unpacked arrays

### Standard Clause

- IEEE 1800-2023: §16.9.4 (pp. 419–422)

### Normative Requirement (<= 40 words)
> "Global clocking past sampled value functions are as follows: $past_gclk, $rose_gclk, $fell_gclk, $stable_gclk, $changed_gclk... Global clocking future sampled value functions are as follows: $future_gclk, $rising_gclk, $falling_gclk, $steady_gclk, $changing_gclk... It shall be an error if any of these functions is called when no global clocking declaration is present."

### Probe File & Observed Result
- Probes: `p16_09_04_all_gclk_funcs.sv`, `p16_09_04_future_gclk.sv`, `neg/n16_09_04_no_global_clock.sv`, `neg/n16_09_04_future_gclk_procedural.sv`, `neg/n16_09_04_nested_future_gclk.sv` (Slurm jobs 3186, 3187, 3190, 3191, commit `c31cbf1b`)
- Observed:
  1. Seven functions (`$past_gclk`, `$changed_gclk`, `$future_gclk`, `$rising_gclk`, `$falling_gclk`, `$steady_gclk`, `$changing_gclk`) are unregistered and fail in VVP with undefined system function errors.
  2. Three functions (`$rose_gclk`, `$fell_gclk`, `$stable_gclk`) are registered in `vpi/sys_sva.c` only as constant compile-progress stubs (`sva_const_calltf`) that unconditionally return 0 without sampling against $global_clock.
  3. Static semantic diagnostics (rejecting calls absent a global clocking declaration, rejecting future functions in procedural code, and rejecting nested future functions) are not performed.

### Expected Behavior
Compiler and VVP runtime must provide functional implementations of all ten global clocking sampled value functions sampling with respect to $global_clock, and enforce static compilation errors for calls absent a global clocking declaration, procedural future calls, and nested future calls.

IEEE 1800-2017 and 2023 §16.4 allow any single subroutine call (including user-defined tasks without illegal output/automatic arguments) as the action statement of an observed (`#0`) deferred assertion, scheduled in the Reactive region.

### Normative Requirement (<= 40 words)

When a `##0` cycle delay executes before the associated clocking event has occurred in the current time step, the calling process must suspend until the clocking event occurs (at time 5 ns).

## Gap

Post-construction procedural reads and writes of coverage instance options `goal` and `comment` are rejected as unsupported. The current compiler supports procedural `weight` and `at_least` access in the tested covergroup, coverpoint, and cross cases, but not these other instance-specific members.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017 §19.7 (p. 579) and IEEE 1800-2023 §19.7 (p. 606) state that other instance-specific options can be assigned procedurally after a covergroup is instantiated. Tables 19-1/19-2 list `goal` and `comment` at covergroup, coverpoint, and cross levels; §19.10 defines the corresponding implicit option structures (2017 pp. 585–586; 2023 pp. 613–614).

## Reproduction

On Icarus 13.0 devel source commit `82023726` (Slurm job 3008), the positive `option.weight`/`option.at_least` probes compile and run in both `-g2017` and `-g2023`. A procedural probe that assigns `cp.option.goal`, assigns `cp.option.comment`, and reads both members fails to compile in both editions with four `sorry: procedural ... option ... is not supported` diagnostics. The negative nonexistent-member probe is rejected as expected. Raw commands and logs are recorded at `evidence/ieee1800-audit-c18-c19-20261019/attempt-18-c19-10/results-3008/` on the audit branch.

## Acceptance

- Support post-construction procedural reads and writes of `goal` and `comment` on covergroup, coverpoint, and cross instances in IEEE 1800-2017 and 2023.
- Preserve the standard's definition-only restrictions on options such as `per_instance`, `auto_bin_max`, and `detect_overlap`.
- Add paired runtime regressions and keep nonexistent option members rejected.
title: [IEEE 1800] §19.10 — Support procedural goal and comment options

## Summary

Icarus fails to elaborate a sampled-value function in a procedural event control when the module declares a default clocking block. IEEE 1800-2017 §16.9.3 permits sampled-value functions in procedural code and infers the default clocking event outside assertions. The default clocking support umbrella issue #17 explicitly left default clocking out of scope.

## Minimal reproducer

```systemverilog
module top;
  logic clk_tb = 0;
  logic signal = 0;
  always #5 clk_tb = ~clk_tb;
  default clocking default_clk @(posedge clk_tb); endclocking
  initial begin
    #2 signal = 1;
    #10 $finish;
  end
  initial forever @($changed(signal)) $display("changed at %0t", $time);
endmodule
```

Compile with `iverilog -g2017 -gassertions -s top default-clocking-changed.sv -o test.vvp`.

## Observed

Pinned Icarus 9b5fad2afb4104caa816b257d5bccc40f01b8c66 (binary SHA-256 `6cd9749cb1e981820f64fdc737ae458bf6c46e3fcad8927afaf92649ee9a3288`) and current main ca559fd97b19bd6a56cc10f0faf8583b4077975f (binary SHA-256 `c99ee9c08468fb20f7635fb3380adb0d620c9037c19c02236a435a61c7be0130`) both fail with `System function $ivl_clocking_sample not defined in system table or SFT file(s)`.

The same behavior is present in five event controls in Caliptra's SoC-IFC testbench. A testbench overlay that samples `$changed` at `@(posedge clk_tb)` compiles and runs, and SoC-IFC row 21 passes with that overlay. Verilator 5.032 does not validate the original form: with timing enabled it reports an internal `Unknown node type ... STABLE` error.

## Expected

Support sampled-value function expressions in procedural event controls using the inferred default clocking event, or emit a direct unsupported-feature diagnostic instead of the unresolved internal system function. Preserve the LRM sampling region semantics.

## Evidence

Reproducer, compiler output, and the passing workaround are retained under `evidence/caliptra-bfm-m17-20261019/diagnostics/socifc-clocking-sample/`.
title: [IEEE 1800] default clocking for sampled-value functions in procedural event controls

body:
## Gap

Clocking-block outputs whose target is an unpacked array of nets are currently rejected. Scalar and packed net clockvar outputs work, and PR #669 covers 1D fixed-unpacked variable outputs, but unpacked net targets need per-element net drivers.

IEEE 1800-2017 and 1800-2023 §14.16.2 require a driver for a net clocking output, initialized to Z and driven from the clocking output's invisible variable in Re-NBA. Multiple clocking outputs and other net drivers must resolve together. The implementation must preserve this behavior for every legal unpacked net element, including resolution with independent drivers.

## Acceptance

- Support the unpacked net target shapes permitted by §14.16.2 in both IEEE 1800-2017 and 1800-2023.
- Create and schedule per-element net drivers with the required initial Z and Re-NBA updates; verify normal net resolution with another driver.
- Add paired 2017/2023 positive and negative/boundary regressions to legacy and JSON/VVP runners.
- Record tested boundaries and evidence in the conformance matrix.

## Related work

- #438 / PR #669 is limited to 1D fixed-unpacked variable outputs and selected targets. This issue tracks unpacked **net** outputs separately.
title: [IEEE 1800] §14.16.2 — Support unpacked net clockvar outputs

body:
## Summary

Pinned Icarus 13.0 rejects a trailing empty positional argument to `$psprintf`. The same compiler builds and runs a control with only that trailing comma/empty argument removed. Verilator 5.032 builds and runs both. The Caliptra KeyVault generated configuration contains the same argument-list shape in a `uvm_info` message. `$psprintf` is non-standard (Verilator emits `NONSTD`), so please classify this compatibility case before choosing a fix.

## Minimal reproducer

`psprintf_empty_arg.sv`:

```systemverilog
module psprintf_empty_arg;
  initial begin
    $display("%s", $psprintf("The agent at '%s' uses %s", "agent", "ifname", ));
    $finish;
  end
endmodule
```

Control `psprintf_control.sv` differs only by removing the last comma and empty argument.

## Results

Icarus reproducer command:

```sh
iverilog -g2017 -s psprintf_empty_arg -o repro-empty.vvp psprintf_empty_arg.sv
```

Pinned Icarus source `9b5fad2afb4104caa816b257d5bccc40f01b8c66`, binary SHA256 `6cd9749cb1e981820f64fdc737ae458bf6c46e3fcad8927afaf92649ee9a3288`:

- Reproducer compile exits 1: `The function $psprintf has been called with missing/empty parameters.`
- Control compile and run exit 0; it prints `The agent at 'agent' uses ifname`.

Verilator 5.032 (Debian 5.032-1): both forms compile and run with exit 0 using `verilator --binary --timing -Wno-fatal --top-module psprintf_empty_arg --Mdir obj_empty psprintf_empty_arg.sv` followed by `obj_empty/Vpsprintf_empty_arg`. The reproducer prints `The agent at 'agent' uses ifname ` (with a trailing space). Verilator warns that `$psprintf` is non-standard.

## Caliptra context

At Caliptra RTL pin `49370266d12cb0c4a8f71b3a0ff7e54ba7d4866e`, `kv_rst_configuration.svh` SHA256 `9d1682590cb85410b67cefe0df3f66f6ca31304f03a1458d283df99411c3a2a6` has the same trailing-empty-argument shape at lines 142–144:

```systemverilog
`uvm_info("CFG",
          $psprintf("The agent at '%s' is using interface named %s has the following parameters: ", agent_path, interface_name, ),
          UVM_DEBUG)
```

The full generated KeyVault compile log reports the error at line 149; the source call is at lines 142–144. The source excerpt and compile log are retained in the local M16 evidence tree.

The reduced source, both Slurm job captures, source context, commands, compiler hashes/versions, and logs are preserved in this directory. This report does not claim a full Caliptra test pass and changes no RTL, firmware, or pass criteria.
title: from-caliptra-dv: classify trailing empty $psprintf argument

Clause: 2017 §19.4 pp.556-557 / 2023 §19.4 pp.578-579 (embedded covergroups); coverpoint sources per §19.5 (2017 p.559 / 2023 p.583); coverage arithmetic per §19.11.1 (2017 p.586 / 2023 p.614); parameterized classes §8.25.
Requirement: "A covergroup declaration within a class is an embedded covergroup declaration. An embedded covergroup declaration declares an anonymous covergroup type and an instance variable of the anonymous type." A specialization of a parameterized class is a class, so its embedded covergroup must collect coverage like a non-parameterized class's.
Probes (exact current main c344d20197a569dea8936bad95de3d185b1e78dc, GCC 15.2, Icarus 13.0 devel; -g2023; -g2017 not run): evidence/issue457-covergroup-inheritance-20261017/attempt-13/parameterized-base-control.sv (class B #(type T = int); T a; covergroup cg; cp: coverpoint a { bins z = {0}; bins nz = {[1:15]}; } endgroup; function new; cg = new; endfunction; B#(int) bi; bi.a = 1; bi.cg.sample()), value-param-control.sv (class B #(parameter int W = 4); bit [W-1:0] a; same covergroup; B#(4)) and type-source-control.sv. Binary hashes: attempt-13/remote-main-c344/results/binaries.sha256.
Observed: every probe compiles and runs with exit 0, but vvp reports malformed %covgrp / sample / dynamic static-class metadata and get_inst_coverage() returns 0.0; the type-parameter-source case also reports a stack_obj cleanup leak. The failure is not limited to a type-parameter-typed source: a value-parameter width and a plain int source in a parameterized class fail the same way. A non-parameterized class with an embedded covergroup, and a non-parameterized class extending B#(int), work (coverage 50.0 expected and observed).
Expected: after sampling a = 1, bins nz is covered and z is not: coverage 50.0 (1 of 2 bins, §19.11.1), with no metadata diagnostics.
Related, distinct scope: #457 (covergroup inheritance, 2023 §19.4.1) covers the extends forms; this issue is the plain embedded covergroup inside a parameterized class.

body:
## Summary

A class method declared as an extern function without an explicit return type, then defined out of class, is rejected by the pinned Icarus build. The equivalent source is accepted by Verilator 5.032. Adding an explicit `void` return type makes both tools accept it.

IEEE Std 1800-2017 §8.24 covers out-of-block method declarations, and §13.4 says an empty implicit function return syntax has a scalar `logic` return type ([standard text](https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf)).

This construct is present in Caliptra's `soc_ifc_tb_pkg.sv` (`lock_fuses` and `unlock_fuses`).

## Minimal reproducer

```systemverilog
package p;
  class C;
    extern function lock_fuses();
  endclass
  function C::lock_fuses();
  endfunction
endpackage
module top;
  import p::*;
  initial begin C c = new(); c.lock_fuses(); end
endmodule
```

## Observed

- Icarus 13.0, source `9b5fad2afb4104caa816b257d5bccc40f01b8c66`, binary SHA256 `6cd9749cb1e981820f64fdc737ae458bf6c46e3fcad8927afaf92649ee9a3288`: `iverilog -g2017 -tnull -s top implicit.sv` exits 3 with `lock_fuses doesn't name a type`.
- Verilator 5.032: `verilator --lint-only --Wno-fatal --top-module top implicit.sv` exits 0 (ignored-return warning only).
- Control with `extern function void lock_fuses();` and `function void C::lock_fuses();` exits 0 on both tools.

The exact sources and command results are saved in the Caliptra BFM M15 evidence tree.
title: Icarus rejects out-of-class extern function with implicit return type

## Summary

A fixed multidimensional unpacked array stored in a struct member is rejected when passed to an ordinary SystemVerilog function with an open-array formal.

## Reproducer

Run from the repository root:

```sh
iverilog -g2012 -s top -o /tmp/open-array.vvp repros/struct_array_member_open_array_io.sv
```

The current main build rejects `sum_md(direct.md)` at `repros/struct_array_member_open_array_io.sv:115` with:

> fixed unpacked-array value and queue/dynamic-array context may differ only in the slowest-varying unpacked dimension and require equivalent element types

The same rejection was reproduced with both the macOS build and the Linux Slurm build at main `9cfce1375`.

## Expected behavior

The fixed array `int md[1:2][7:5]` should be accepted as an actual for `input int a[][]`, and the function should observe both dimensions and their declared bounds. The reproducer also checks values and geometry.

This is ordinary SystemVerilog function argument compatibility, distinct from the DPI open-array coverage in `tests/m4b_struct_array_member_open_test.sv`.

## Scope

Feature work: investigate multidimensional fixed unpacked-array actuals for open-array formals, including struct-member selection. Keep the reproducer as a regression test once supported.
title: [IEEE 1800] §7.4 — Accept multidimensional fixed arrays as open-array actuals

## Summary

Icarus c339 leaves an enum member at its zero value in a packed-struct assignment pattern when another member is assigned an expression wider than that member. In the reproducer, `rd_wr_en` stays `RW_IDLE` although the pattern explicitly assigns `RW_READ`.

## Minimal reproducer

[Self-contained SystemVerilog test](https://github.com/QD-EDA/qd-bfm/blob/61b1e83/evidence/caliptra-bfm-environment-matrix-20261011/reproducers/icarus-struct-assignment-width/self-contained.sv)

The type is:

```systemverilog
typedef enum logic [1:0] {RW_IDLE = 2'b00, RW_READ = 2'b01} mode_t;
typedef struct packed { mode_t rd_wr_en; logic [13:0] addr; } mem_if_t;
```

The failing assignment is `bad <= '{rd_wr_en: RW_READ, addr: locked_src_addr + num_mem_operands};`, where the address operands are 14 and 32 bits. The control assignment explicitly sized to 14 bits produces the expected packed value.

## Observed

With Icarus source revision `c339b9f2287a743aeb7ab6de6528e8d34a4dd602`:

```text
bad=0002 bad_en=00 bad_addr=0002
```

The sized control gives `good=4002 good_en=01 good_addr=0002`. Verilator 5.051 produces `bad=4002 bad_en=01`, matching the control. Logs and binary hashes are in the linked evidence directory.

This also affects the pinned Adams Bridge `sigencode_z_top.sv`: request assignment patterns combine the `RW_READ` control field with a 32-bit counter expression assigned to a 14-bit address member. Its testbench then reports 3,584 mismatches with unknown outputs and no output-memory writes.

IEEE 1800-2017 §10.9.2 says assignment-pattern member expressions are evaluated in the context of the corresponding member type: https://fpga.mit.edu/6205/_static/F25/documentation/1800-2017.pdf

Related closed issues #19 and #41 cover broader struct/pattern work and struct defaults, but I did not find this member-context-sizing behavior described there.
title: Packed struct assignment pattern member loses enum value with wider sibling expression

## Measurement

A pinned Caliptra top-level run on Icarus c339 progressed from trace cycle 100 to 25,700 before its 3,500-second guard expired. That is 25,600 cycles over 3,500 seconds, or 7.31 effective cycles per wall-second. The wall duration is from the whole firmware runner, including setup, so this is a conservative end-to-end rate rather than a VVP-only rate.

Sources:
- Icarus: `c339b9f2287a743aeb7ab6de6528e8d34a4dd602`
- Caliptra: `49370266d12cb0c4a8f71b3a0ff7e54ba7d4866e`
- Run: QD-BFM `rand_test_dma`, one iteration, seed 1, trace enabled; runner exit 124 at the 3,500-second timeout.
- Trace log: `evidence/caliptra-bfm-fulltop-rand-dma-reset-c339-20261010/job-242/completed-runs/trace-1/output/trace-1/rand_test_dma/sim.log`
- Resource/exit records: `evidence/caliptra-bfm-fulltop-rand-dma-reset-c339-20261010/job-242/completed-runs/trace-1/logs/resource.log` and `runner-status.txt`

## Suite projection

The current Caliptra test matrix contains 271 active YAML rows. Scaling this 25,600-cycle segment at the measured effective rate gives about 3,500 seconds per row and 948,500 seconds (10.98 days) for 271 rows. This rough projection assumes each row requires one segment of similar size; actual test lengths vary, and this timed-out run did not reach a terminal testcase result.

This throughput makes a full firmware sweep impractical on the current Icarus build. Please profile and identify the dominant simulator/runtime costs so we can plan a feasible qualification path.
title: Caliptra firmware throughput on Icarus c339 projects about 11 days for 271 tests

## IEEE clauses

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§19.5.2–19.5.3 define transition-bin families and §19.11.3 defines type coverage with `type_option.merge_instances=1`. Official edition records: [1800-2017](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/6700/) and [1800-2023](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/7743/).

## Validation question

The current merged-cross reducers cover named and arrayed transition-bin identities, and `sv_covergroup_transition_repeat` covers a 1,000-member compact transition family at instance scope. The recorded V05 residual still calls out transition-family cardinality in merged type coverage as unqualified. No wrong percentage has been reproduced yet, so this issue asks for a narrow standards check and paired reducer; it does not assert a confirmed runtime defect.

Candidate shape:

```systemverilog
covergroup cg with function sample(bit [3:0] value);
  type_option.merge_instances = 1;
  cp: coverpoint value {
    bins wait_bins[] = (12 => 0 [*1:1000] => 13);
  }
endgroup
```

Instantiate two instances of this type, complete selected repetition lengths in each, and compare the merged type percentage with the union of standard bin identities. Include same-bin hits across instances and distinct arrayed-bin hits; verify the denominator and behavior after instance retirement. The candidate is not yet a failure reproducer.

## Acceptance criteria

- Confirm the IEEE identity and denominator rules for arrayed/repeated transition bins under merged type coverage.
- Add strict 2017/2023 tests that establish same-identity sharing, distinct-identity union, and stable coverage after an instance retires.
- If the paired reducer shows a mismatch, fix it and retain a minimized reproducer; otherwise record the clean evidence and close this validation issue.

Related baseline evidence: `sv_covergroup_transition_repeat`, `sv_covergroup_merged_cross_transition`, and the V05 section in `docs/conformance/BLOCKERS.md`. This is separate from #512's Cartesian cross-size resource boundary.

## Gap

The compiler accepts `output` and `inout` as covergroup constructor formals. IEEE 1800-2017 and IEEE 1800-2023 §19.3 require both directions to be illegal for a covergroup formal. Legal `input` and `ref` formals must remain accepted; `ref` is read-only and tracks the actual variable for sampling.

## Reproducer

Run each declaration separately in strict `-g2017` and `-g2023` mode:

```systemverilog
module t;
  int value;
  covergroup cg(output int arg);
    cp: coverpoint arg;
  endgroup
  cg c;
  initial c = new(value);
endmodule
```

Replace `output` with `inout` for the second negative case. The clean `origin/main` install at `af89cfc50be1084cc86c48865f3f6ba78d4512fa` accepted and ran both forms in both editions without a diagnostic. The standalone legal-`ref` sampling behavior is tracked separately in [#448](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/issues/448).

## IEEE basis

IEEE Std 1800-2017 §19.3 and IEEE Std 1800-2023 §19.3 state that `output` or `inout` is illegal as a covergroup formal argument. See the official [2017 standard record](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/6700/) and [2023 standard record](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/7743/).

## Acceptance criteria

- Reject covergroup declarations with `output` or `inout` formals in strict 2017 and 2023 modes.
- Keep legal `input` and `ref` formals accepted, with live read-only `ref` sampling behavior covered under #448.
- Add registered positive and negative tests to the legacy and JSON runners, with exact diagnostics checked in both editions.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §19.3 — Reject output/inout covergroup formals

body:
## IEEE requirement

IEEE 1800-2017 and IEEE 1800-2023 Annex H §H.7.8 permits unpacked aggregate arguments for imported and exported DPI subroutines. Annex H §H.8.2 excludes open-array arguments from exports, but otherwise permits the same formal argument types as imports; fixed-size unpacked arrays are therefore legal. See the official [IEEE 1800-2017](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/6700/) and [IEEE 1800-2023](https://standards.ieee.org/ieee/1800/7743/) standard pages.

## Gap and evidence

The compiler drops an exported function with a legal fixed-size unpacked formal instead of generating a callable C stub. The current-main reducer `tests/negative/m10_dpi_export_fixed_array_argument.sv` reports that the fixed unpacked array argument is unsupported for DPI export. A compact reproducer is:

```systemverilog
module fixed_array_export;
  function int first_value(input int values[2]);
    return values[0];
  endfunction
  export "DPI-C" function first_value;
endmodule
```

On the existing current-main install, `iverilog -g2012 -o /tmp/ieee-census-export.vvp <reducer>` exits nonzero with the targeted “fixed unpacked array argument ... is not yet supported for DPI export; the export is dropped” diagnostic.

## Acceptance criteria

- Generate and link an export stub for legal fixed-size unpacked array formals in strict 2017 and 2023 modes.
- Use the correct direct-reference C ABI and preserve array shape, values, and input/output/inout copy semantics.
- Add an external C caller test covering at least a fixed-size integer array and a packed-element or multidimensional array, with round-trip checks for supported directions.
- Continue to reject exported open-array formals, which Annex H §H.8.2 prohibits.

## Dependencies

Extend the existing scalar and packed-vector export-stub path to fixed unpacked aggregate formals. This is independent of imported shortreal array support and must not relax the exported-open-array rejection.

## Gap

A wide unsigned index into a fixed string array is narrowed to a signed 64-bit address before the bounds check. Values such as `1 << 100` therefore alias element zero instead of returning the string default for an invalid read.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  string words[2] = '{"first", "second"};
  logic [127:0] index = 128'd1 << 100;
  string got;
  initial begin
    got = words[index];
    $display("got='%s'", got);
  end
endmodule
```

Expected `got=''`; the current string-load path narrows the address and can return `words[0]`. The paired 32-bit/100-bit index matrix and exact current path are recorded in [DD-029](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-029--wide-fixed-string-array-reads-alias-a-valid-element).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §7.4.6 requires the element-type default value for an invalid fixed-array read; an invalid wide index must not alias an in-range element.

## Acceptance

- Preserve full index width and signedness through bounds checking for string-array reads.
- Return the default string for out-of-range, negative, and unknown indices without reading or modifying an in-range element.
- Add paired 2017/2023 tests for 32-, 64-, and 128-bit signed/unsigned indices and neighboring valid indices.

## Dependencies

None known. Keep the string-array behavior separate from #414's packed bit-select bounds.
title: [IEEE 1800] §7.4.6 — Preserve wide unsigned indices on fixed string-array reads

## Gap

Increment/decrement of a fixed unpacked-array element compiles but crashes VVP for integral arrays; real-array forms fail to update the element and index. The selected element must be updated once, and postfix must return its old value.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  int a[2] = '{5, 7};
  int idx = 0;
  int old_value;
  initial begin
    old_value = a[idx++]++;
    $display("idx=%0d a0=%0d a1=%0d old=%0d", idx, a[0], a[1], old_value);
  end
endmodule
```

Expected: `idx=1 a0=6 a1=7 old=5`. Current paired strict runs of the function reducer terminate with signal 11; the expanded matrix also shows eight failing real-array runs. See [DD-027](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-027--runtime-increment-of-a-fixed-array-element-crashes-vvp).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§7.4.6 and 11.4.2 define invalid array-index reads and increment/decrement expression behavior.

## Acceptance

- Update fixed-array element storage for pre/post `++` and `--` on integral and real element types.
- Evaluate dynamic indices once and preserve bounds/default behavior.
- Preserve postfix/prefix values and nonselected elements in paired runtime tests.

## Dependencies

None known. This is separate from #498's packed-select carrier updates.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§7.4.6/11.4.2 — Update fixed-array elements for increment expressions

## Gap

VPI source-location properties are hardcoded to zero or absent for ordinary signal/net/reg objects, part-selects, and class variables. These handles correspond to source objects and are covered by the standard location-property requirement.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module top;
  logic signal;
  initial begin
    signal = 1;
  end
endmodule
```

A VPI callback that looks up `top.signal`, calls `vpi_get(vpiLineNo, handle)` and `vpi_get_str(vpiFile, handle)`, currently observes line 0 / no source file. The same gap exists for bit/part-select and class-variable handles. Source audit identifies hardcoded `0` in `__vpiSignal` / `__vpiPV` / `__vpiCobjectVar`; see [DD-049](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd049--vpilineno-vpifile-never-captured-for-signals-part-selects-or-class-variables) and its reproduced VPI probe.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §37.3.3 makes `vpiLineNo` and `vpiFile` applicable to every object corresponding to a source object, except a specific list that does not include signals, selects, or class variables. The properties must also respect the `line` compiler directive.

## Acceptance

- Capture and report source file/line for signals, nets, part/bit selects, and class variables.
- Preserve `line` directive remapping and correctly handle generated/source-derived objects.
- Add VPI tests for each object kind and assert both location properties, with exception-type controls.

## Dependencies

This is a cross-layer source-location feature: elaboration metadata must reach netlist/VVP object creation. Scope the supported source-object set explicitly; do not treat the existing hardcoded zeros as conforming.
title: [IEEE 1800] §37.3.3 — Report source file and line for VPI source objects

A missing task called through an unindexed module-instance scope can compile with a warning and execute later statements, treating the call as a no-op. Missing hierarchical task references must fail lookup; valid calls through the same hierarchy must continue to work.

## Gap

A matching-width increment of a packed bit/part select reaches the VVP backend and aborts on a vector-width assertion. The update must use the selected width, return the correct prefix/postfix value, and preserve bits outside the selection.

A package-qualified static class method call works in statement position after the related call-form repair, but remains rejected in expression position.

## Gap

The procedural sampled-history implementation evaluates `$past` operands when its helper process runs in the Active region. If a writer runs first on the same sampling edge, the captured value is the new Active-region value instead of the required Preponed sample.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  bit clk = 0;
  int d = 0, k = 0;
  always #5 clk = !clk;
  always @(negedge clk) begin k++; d = k; end
  always @(negedge clk) $display("past=%0d", $past(d));
endmodule
```

With the writer declared first, current behavior reports the current edge’s value rather than the value sampled before Active updates. The paired writer-first evidence is in [DD-104](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-104--procedural-past-history-captures-the-active-region-value-not-the-preponed-value).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§16.5.1 and 16.9.3 specify Preponed-region sampling for assertion sampled values.

## Acceptance

- Capture supported procedural `$past` operands before Active-region writers on the sampling event.
- Preserve reader-first/writer-first order independence and history enable behavior.
- Add paired tests for inferred, explicit-event, and default-clocking paths, with explicit diagnostics for unsupported operand shapes.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§16.5.1/16.9.3 — Sample procedural `$past` operands in the Preponed region

body:
## Gap

Dynamic packed ranges on a class property lack the selected carrier needed to implement partial out-of-bounds reads and writes. The current implementation rejects uncertain crossing ranges rather than providing the standard’s bit-level clipping, while the ordinary-signal path already has partial-range behavior.

## Reproducer shape

```systemverilog
class C; logic [1:0][7:0] value; endclass
module t;
  C obj = new;
  integer base;
  initial begin
    base = 6;
    obj.value[0][base +: 4] = 4'hf;
    $display("%h", obj.value);
  end
endmodule
```

The paired evidence distinguishes in-range and crossing class-property selectors and records that the bounded-only acceptance does not qualify clipping. See [DD-103](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-103--exact-clipping-for-a-dynamic-inner-packed-class-property-range).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §11.5.1: partial out-of-range reads produce X only for missing bits; writes update only in-range bits.

## Acceptance

- Preserve inner packed-dimension bounds for dynamic class-property reads and writes.
- Clip partial reads/writes with correct X/write behavior for blocking, compound, and nonblocking assignments.
- Preserve single index evaluation and ascending/descending direction.
- Add paired in-range, partial-crossing, wholly out-of-range, unknown-index, and truncation cases.

## Dependencies

Related to #471 for packed carrier bounds, but class-property read-modify-write lowering needs its own implementation and tests.

## Gap

A legal `release` of a selected packed subfield aborts target generation instead of producing a simulator diagnostic or executing the release. Releasing the whole packed aggregate and a whole member works.

## Reproducer and evidence

```systemverilog
module t;
  logic [1:0][7:0] value;
  initial begin
    force value[0][3:0] = 4'hf;
    release value[0][3:0];
  end
endmodule
```

The paired strict compile aborts at the VVP target assertion in `show_stmt_release`; the focused source and controls are recorded in [DD-088](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-088--packed-subfield-release-asserts-on-non-immediate-lhs-offset).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §10.6 defines procedural continuous assignment and `release` with a `variable_lvalue`; selected packed lvalues are within the standard lvalue grammar.

## Acceptance

- Generate correct release behavior for supported selected packed lvalues without aborting `ivl`.
- Preserve other packed bits and the distinction between whole-object and selected releases.
- Add paired force/release runtime cases for constant and dynamic packed offsets.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §10.6 — Release selected packed subfields without a target assertion

```systemverilog
endmodule
```

## Acceptance

- Connect a compatible unpacked-array slice to an output port and propagate each driven element.
- Preserve declared dimensions, index direction, and whole-array connections.

body:
## Gap

A solve-before target selecting a queue element inside a fixed-array class property is lowered to the scalar fixed-array slot. The source compiles and randomization succeeds, but the requested ordering is not applied to the queue element.

## Reproducer and evidence

```systemverilog
class C;
  rand bit first;
  rand bit values[2][$];
  constraint c { solve first before values[0][0]; }
endclass
```

The current runtime emits a scalar element target; a control targeting queue contents is rejected rather than represented. See [DD-085](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-085--whole-selected-queue-masquerades-as-a-scalar-solve-order-target).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.10 and 1800-2023 §18.5.9 define variable ordering; both editions include queue size/orderable random variables in this domain.

## Acceptance

- Preserve the selected queue-element identity for solve-before targets below fixed array ranks.
- Reject unsupported target shapes explicitly; do not silently remap them to a neighboring scalar.
- Add paired solver and emitted-target checks with fixed arrays, queues, and legal controls.

## Dependencies

Related to the container randomization family in #419, but this selected-target identity gap needs independent coverage.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§18.5.10/18.5.9 — Preserve solve-before targets in fixed-array queues

## Gap

A fixed-array class property accepts `.reverse()` but emits a runtime warning and leaves the array unchanged. The same operation works on an ordinary fixed-array receiver.

## Reproducer and evidence

```systemverilog
class C; int values[3] = '{1,2,3}; endclass
module t;
  initial begin C obj = new; obj.values.reverse(); $display("%p", obj.values); end
endmodule
```

The property receiver is skipped; the paired strict failure and fixed-array control are recorded in [DD-084](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-084--fixed-class-property-ordering-method-silently-skips-its-receiver).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §7.12.2 permits ordering methods on unpacked fixed and dynamic arrays, excluding associative arrays.

## Acceptance

- Apply `.reverse()` and the other applicable ordering methods to fixed-array class properties with correct copyback.
- Preserve receiver values on method errors and keep associative-array restrictions.
- Add paired fixed local/property, ascending/descending, and method-family controls.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §7.12.2 — Apply ordering methods to fixed class-property arrays

body:
## Gap

A four-state X literal in a constraint is lowered as zero. Randomization then reports success with zero instead of rejecting the illegal constraint.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
class C;
  rand logic [3:0] en;
  constraint c { en == 4'hx; }
endclass
module t;
  initial begin C obj = new; $display("ok=%0d value=%h", obj.randomize(), obj.en); end
endmodule
```

The strict 2017/2023 reducer reports wrong success with value zero. A packed-struct member control fails the same way. See [DD-083](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-083--xz-numeric-literal-in-a-constraint-can-alias-zero).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §18.3 states constraints support only two-state values; X/Z values and four-state operators are illegal and shall result in an error.

## Acceptance

- Diagnose X/Z-valued constraint expressions rather than discarding their unknown bits.
- Preserve valid two-state constraints and unrelated four-state procedural expressions.
- Add paired scalar, array-member, X, Z, and four-state-operator negative cases.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §18.3 — Diagnose four-state values in constraints
