## Gap

Indexed part-selects on ascending packed class properties select the wrong bits, while copying the same property to a local packed variable and selecting it there gives the expected values.

## Reproducer and evidence

The strict reducer `class C; bit [0:7] value = 8'hA6; endclass` compares `obj.value[2+:3]` and `obj.value[5-:3]` against selections from a local copy. The class-property route returns different bits in both editions although the stored value is unchanged. See [DD-081](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-081--ascending-packed-class-property-indexed-read-selects-wrong-bits).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §11.5.1 defines indexed part-select base, width, and declared-direction mapping.

## Acceptance

- Return the same selected bits through class-property and local packed-variable paths for `+:` and `-:`.
- Cover ascending and descending declarations, dynamic bases, and boundary cases in paired editions.
- Keep out-of-range result semantics separately covered by #414 and #471.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §11.5.1 — Preserve indexed part-select orientation on ascending class properties

body:
## Gap

Several legal `foreach` forms silently skip packed ranks or lose effects from a selected parent path: a queue of packed elements `foreach (q[i,j])`, a packed child after an omitted associative key `foreach (map[,bank,bit_index])`, and a selected parent such as `foreach (boxes[next_idx()].m[,bank])`.

## Reproducers

```systemverilog
bit [1:0] q[$];
initial begin q.push_back(2'b11); foreach (q[i,j]) $display("%0d %0d", i, j); end
```

The current queue form visits zero bodies. The omitted-associative-key packed-tail form currently diagnoses as unsupported; the indexed-parent form drops `next_idx()` evaluation. Paired strict evidence and Slang controls are linked from [DD-077](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-077--queue-foreach-silently-skips-a-packed-element-dimension), [DD-079](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-079--packed-child-rank-after-an-omitted-associative-foreach-key), and [DD-080](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-080--indexed-parent-path-before-an-omitted-associative-foreach-key).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §12.7.3 defines loop variables for each array dimension, including packed and unpacked dimensions; omitted variables skip iteration only for their corresponding dimension.

## Acceptance

- Iterate queue element packed dimensions and packed ranks after skipped associative dimensions.
- Preserve each dimension’s index type, bounds, and declared direction.
- Evaluate selected parent expressions according to their normal observable semantics; do not silently drop them.
- Add paired runtime tests with discriminating values and side effects for all three shapes.

## Dependencies

None known. The fixed associative-array element representation in #484 is separate.
title: [IEEE 1800] §12.7.3 — Traverse packed ranks after runtime and omitted array dimensions

body:
## Gap

Reading a nonexistent associative-array entry returns the right default value but emits no warning. The warning must distinguish an implicit element default from a user-specified default, which suppresses it.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  int values[int];
  initial begin
    $display("value=%0d exists=%0d", values[9], values.exists(9));
  end
endmodule
```

The current runtime prints the default and `exists=0` without a warning. See the minimal paired evidence in [DD-071](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-071--missing-associative-key-read-omits-the-required-warning).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §7.8.6 requires a warning for reading a nonexistent entry; a user-specified default suppresses the warning.

## Acceptance

- Warn on reads of missing entries without a user-specified default, while returning the element type's default value.
- Do not allocate the entry on a read.
- Suppress the warning for user-defaulted associative arrays; warn on invalid write indices as required.
- Add paired read, existence, user-default, and invalid-write cases.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §7.8.6 — Warn when reading a nonexistent associative entry

body:
## Gap

A dynamic array or queue used as a fixed-array associative-map pattern value is rejected at compile time, even when its runtime size matches. For mismatches, the required runtime error must leave the existing map unchanged; the current typed pattern path does not preserve destination layout through replacement.

## Evidence

The paired strict expected-compile-fail fixture [`sv_assoc_fixed_pattern_variable_source_fail.v`](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/ivtest/ivltests/sv_assoc_fixed_pattern_variable_source_fail.v) and the transactional module/class reducers documented in [DD-072](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-072--variable-size-whole-map-pattern-items-need-transactional-validation) show the current unsupported diagnostic and the legal matching-size cases accepted by Slang.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§7.6 and 7.8 define assignment compatibility and associative-array assignment patterns.

## Acceptance

- Accept a variable-size value when its runtime dimensions match the fixed-array element type.
- On mismatch, report the required runtime error and preserve the prior map contents without partial replacement.
- Add paired tests for matching/mismatching dynamic-array and queue values, default/keyed items, and module/class maps.

## Dependencies

Requires fixed-array associative element support tracked by #484.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§7.6/7.8 — Validate variable-size associative pattern values transactionally

body:
## Gap

Associative arrays whose element type is a fixed unpacked array are rejected in both strict editions. Removing the type guard alone is unsafe: the runtime must retain the fixed bounds and default element construction for each key.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  bit values[int][2];
  initial begin
    values[4][0] = 1'b1;
    $display("value=%b", values[4][0]);
  end
endmodule
```

A three-line strict reducer fails to compile on the frozen baseline while Slang accepts it. The implementation boundary and focused paired evidence are in [DD-067](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-067--associative-arrays-of-fixed-arrays-lack-a-sound-vvp-representation).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§7.4 and 7.8 define unpacked and associative arrays; the associative element type may be a fixed unpacked array.

## Acceptance

- Preserve fixed dimensions and value construction for associative entries.
- Support reads and whole-element writes, indexed class-handle leaves, packed-bit writes after the fixed rank, and nonblocking indexed writes.
- Add paired module-scope and class-property tests for absent/present keys and retain bounds/default behavior.

## Dependencies

None known. Variable-size assignment-pattern values and transactional rollback are tracked separately in #485.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§7.4/7.8 — Support associative arrays with fixed-array elements

body:
## Gap

A `const ref` actual forwarded to another `const ref` formal is diagnosed as an assignment to a const signal. The binding is read-only reference forwarding, not a write to the actual.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
task automatic inner(const ref logic [7:0] x); endtask
task automatic outer(const ref logic [7:0] x);
  inner(x);
endtask
module t;
  logic [7:0] value;
  initial outer(value);
endmodule
```

Icarus rejects the calls with `Assignment to const signal`; Slang accepts them in both editions and rejects forwarding to a writable `ref`. See [DD-066](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-066--const-ref-forwarding-is-rejected-as-an-assignment-to-const).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §13.5.2 defines pass-by-reference and permits const-ref formal arguments; binding one to another must preserve constness without treating it as assignment.

## Acceptance

- Permit compatible const-ref-to-const-ref forwarding.
- Keep writable-ref binding to a const actual illegal.
- Add paired forwarding, type-mismatch, and writable-ref negative controls.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §13.5.2 — Allow const-ref forwarding to const-ref formals

body:
## Gap

Calling `vif.cg.sample()` compiles but samples zero coverpoints for the bound interface instances. The equivalent physical calls `u0.cg.sample()` and `u1.cg.sample()` update coverage, so the loss is specific to virtual-interface receiver metadata.

## Reproducer shape

```systemverilog
interface bus_if(input logic clk);
  logic value;
  covergroup cg @(posedge clk);
    coverpoint value;
  endgroup
  cg cov = new;
endinterface
module t;
  // Bind a virtual bus_if handle to an instance, then call vif.cov.sample().
endmodule
```

The paired strict reducer shows 0% through a virtual receiver and 50% through the physical-instance control; Slang accepts both editions. See [DD-065](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-065--virtual-interface-covergroup-sampling-silently-has-zero-coverpoints).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §19.3 defines covergroup sampling; §25.9 defines virtual-interface access to interface members.

## Acceptance

- Retain the virtual-interface receiver and use its covergroup metadata and sample expressions at runtime.
- Handle rebinding between interface instances correctly.
- Add paired direct, virtual, and rebound-handle coverage checks; do not accept silent zero-point sampling.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§19.3/25.9 — Sample covergroups through virtual interfaces

body:
## Gap

X/Z samples are converted to numeric zero before ordinary value-bin matching, so a known-only bin incorrectly receives coverage from an unknown sample.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  logic flag;
  covergroup cg;
    cp: coverpoint flag { bins known = {0, 1}; }
  endgroup
  cg c = new;
  initial begin
    flag = 1'bx; c.sample();
    $display("coverage=%0f", c.get_inst_coverage());
  end
endmodule
```

Expected coverage remains 0%; the current runtime reports 50% after X. Paired strict evidence for X/Z value and expression samples is linked from [DD-063](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-063--covergroup-sampling-loses-xz-before-ordinary-bin-matching) and [DD-096](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-096--xz-coverpoint-samples-hit-known-value-bins).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §19.5.4 specifies four-state value-bin matching and excludes X/Z samples from wildcard bins. Ordinary bins with known-only values must not match X/Z as zero.

## Acceptance

- Preserve the four-state sampled value through ordinary and wildcard matching.
- Keep explicit X/Z bins matchable with four-state comparison; exclude X/Z only where the LRM requires it.
- Add paired scalar, expression, X, Z, and wildcard-bin cases.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §19.5.4 — Preserve four-state values during coverage bin matching

body:
## Gap

`$system` accepts two arguments without an arity diagnostic even though both standard editions allow at most one optional string expression.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  initial $system("exit 0", "exit 7");
endmodule
```

Strict 2017 and 2023 compiles currently succeed. The paired invalid-source logs are documented in [DD-062](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-062--system-accepts-an-extra-argument).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017 §20.18.1 and 1800-2023 §20.17.1 specify zero or one string argument.

## Acceptance

- Diagnose calls with more than one argument during compilation.
- Preserve zero-argument and one-string-argument calls and their return behavior.
- Add paired positive and negative arity tests.

## Dependencies

None known; separate from runtime result support.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§20.18.1/20.17.1 — Reject excess `$system` arguments

body:
## Gap

An inline constraint containing `this.no_such_member` is accepted when that name exists only in the caller class. Explicit `this` must resolve in the class of the randomized object; an absent target member is an error.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
class target; rand int value; endclass
class caller;
  int no_such_member;
  target obj;
  initial begin end
endclass
```

In the caller’s `run` method, `obj.randomize() with { this.no_such_member == 1; }` currently compiles without an error. The exact paired strict reproducer and logs are in [DD-060](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-060--explicit-this-inline-target-lookup-accepts-a-caller-only-member).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §18.7 specifies inline constraint lookup in the context of the randomized object.

## Acceptance

- Resolve explicit `this` only against the randomized object’s class scope.
- Diagnose an explicit target member absent from that class, even if the caller has a homonym.
- Preserve valid target members and bare-name lookup rules in paired editions.

## Dependencies

None known; separate from #478's active-object alias handling.
title: [IEEE 1800] §18.7 — Bind explicit `this` in inline constraints to the target class

body:
## Gap

An inline constraint that refers to a second handle aliasing the randomized object treats that reference as caller state. The invoked object’s active random variables must remain the solve targets even when referenced through an alias.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
class item;
  rand int clen;
endclass
class owner;
  item req, alt;
endclass
module t;
  initial begin
    owner o = new; o.req = new; o.alt = o.req;
    o.alt.randomize() with { req.clen == 12; };
    $display("clen=%0d", o.req.clen);
  end
endmodule
```

The direct receiver control succeeds, but the aliased receiver returns failure and leaves `clen` zero in paired strict runs. A distinct object handle correctly remains caller state. See [DD-059](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-059--inline-constraints-capture-an-aliased-active-random-variable-as-caller-state).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017 §18.5.9 and 1800-2023 §18.5.8 define active random variables from the invoked object; §18.7 governs inline constraint lookup.

## Acceptance

- Identify active random variables by the randomized object's identity, including aliases.
- Preserve caller-state behavior for references to distinct objects.
- Add paired tests for direct handles, aliased handles, nested aliases, and distinct objects.

## Dependencies

None known; this is separate from #419's unsupported nested random-container shapes.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§18.5.9/18.7 — Resolve inline constraint aliases by object identity

body:
## Gap

Both strict editions accept a `ref logic [31:0]` formal bound to a `bit [31:0]` actual. Reference arguments require equivalent types; assignment conversion is not permitted for `ref` binding.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
task automatic take(ref logic [31:0] value); endtask
module t;

endmodule
```

The source currently compiles in both editions. See paired logs and the type-equivalence analysis in [DD-058](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-058--mismatched-two-statefour-state-ref-actual-is-accepted).

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§13.5.2 and 6.22.2(c): ref arguments shall have equivalent data types and are not cast.

## Acceptance

- Preserve acceptance of equivalent types and valid `const ref` forwarding.
- Add paired legal and illegal cases for task and function arguments.

None known. Separate from #449's `ref static` storage duration.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§13.5.2/6.22.2 — Reject non-equivalent ref actual types

body:
## Gap

Sequence match-item assignments accept only a bare local-variable name. Standard `operator_assignment` lvalues with a part-select or bit-select are rejected, preventing a local accumulator from being assembled over successive sequence matches.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
property p(input logic [3:0] src);
  logic [7:0] acc;
  (1'b1, acc[3:0] = src) ##1 (1'b1, acc[7:4] = src) ##1 (acc == {src, src});
endproperty
```

The current parser rejects the selected left-hand side. [DD-035](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-035--sequence-match-item-assignment-lhs-is-a-bare-identifier-only-no-part-bit-select-2026-09-16) records paired reducers, grammar evidence, and the required read-modify-write semantics.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 Annex A.2.10 defines sequence match items using `operator_assignment`; the variable-lvalue grammar admits selected lvalues.

## Acceptance

- Accept bit-select and part-select local-variable lvalues in match-item assignments.
- Preserve untouched bits with ordered read-modify-write semantics across later match steps.
- Add functional paired-edition tests for both selected forms and the original accumulator use case.

## Dependencies

None known; do not treat grammar acceptance alone as completion.
title: [IEEE 1800] §16 — Support selected lvalues in sequence match-item assignments

body:
## Gap

A property with both integral `int` and packed `logic` local declarations parses, but the `int` local is not materialized for later match-item use.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
property p;
  int a;
  logic [3:0] z;
  (1'b1, a = 1) ##1 (1'b1, z = a[3:0]) ##1 (z == 4'd1);
endproperty
```

The current compiler reports it cannot bind `a[...]`; declarations of only one kind work. Slang accepts this form. Evidence and same-kind controls are in [DD-034](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-034--mixing-int-and-logic-assertion-local-variable-declarations-in-one-property-breaks-binding-2026-09-16).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §16.10 defines local variables in sequences and properties; §16.12 defines their use in assertion expressions.

## Acceptance

- Materialize mixed integral and packed local declarations in a single property with the correct types and scope.
- Preserve same-type declarations and reject invalid declarations with ordinary diagnostics.
- Add paired 2017/2023 runtime tests that check values across match steps.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §16 — Bind mixed-type assertion-local declarations consistently

body:
## Gap

A fixed unpacked-array parameter initialized with a fully keyed assignment pattern is rejected. Accepting the pattern also needs correct element lookup: a recorded attempted partial fix caused an assertion when selecting `TABLE[0]`, so a parser/elaboration-only acceptance is insufficient.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
package p;
  typedef bit [7:0] bytes_t[2];
  parameter bytes_t TABLE = '{0:8'h11, 1:8'h22};
  localparam bit [7:0] FIRST = TABLE[0];
endpackage
```

The current baseline rejects the keyed parameter value. See [DD-033](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-033--package-scope-fixed-unpacked-array-parameter-with-a-keyed-assignment-pattern-value-2026-09-16) for the minimal strict Slang control and the element-select failure from an incomplete fix.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§10.9 and 6.22.3 define assignment patterns and array assignment compatibility for fixed unpacked arrays.

## Acceptance

- Support keyed and positional patterns, defaults, direct-scope and wildcard-imported parameters.
- Correctly index accepted array parameters without an assertion or scalar-value fallback.
- Add paired positive and malformed-pattern regressions and retain focused diagnostics for invalid forms.

## Dependencies

None known.
title: [IEEE 1800] §§10.9/6.22 — Elaborate fixed-array parameter assignment patterns and element reads

body:
## Gap

An assignment expression retains X bits when its value is assigned to a two-state destination, even though the equivalent sequence of ordinary assignments converts the X bits to zero.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  bit [3:0] i, j;
  initial begin
    j = (i = 4'bx101);
    $display("i=%b j=%b", i, j);
  end
endmodule
```

Expected output is `i=0101 j=0101`; the recorded runtime result contains unknown bits. Ordinary statements `i=4'bx101; j=i;` produce the expected value. See [DD-026](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-026--two-state-assignment-expression-retains-unknown-bits-at-runtime).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §§11.3 and 6.11 require assignment-expression destination typing and conversion of X/Z to zero for two-state integral types.

## Acceptance

- Apply the destination's two-state conversion to the value of assignment expressions at runtime.
- Preserve four-state destinations and ordinary assignment behavior.
- Add paired 2017/2023 tests for scalar, packed, nested, and selected destinations.

title: [IEEE 1800] §§6.11/11.3 — Convert assignment-expression results to two-state destinations

## Gap

The compiler rejects legal mixed-driver source when one fixed packed element is procedurally written through a dynamic subpart and a different fixed element is continuously driven. The fixed disjoint prefixes are legal; the dynamic selection within one element should not widen the conflict to the whole array.

## Reproducer shape

```systemverilog
module t(input logic d, input logic [3:0] value);
  logic [1:0][7:0] words;
  assign words[1] = 8'h00;
  always_comb words[0][d +: 1] = value[0];
endmodule
```

The focused source is recorded under [DD-021](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-021--dynamic-subpart-of-a-disjoint-mixed-driver-element-is-rejected). Keep the conservative rejection until the selected-element bounds are preserved by #471.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §6.5 permits different driver kinds for variables with disjoint longest static prefixes. The selected elements here have disjoint fixed prefixes.

## Acceptance

- Accept mixed-driver declarations when the statically selected prefixes are disjoint, including a dynamic subpart inside one selected packed element.
- Continue rejecting overlapping prefixes and preserve the full dynamic-index bounds behavior covered by #471.
- Add paired legal/illegal compile cases and runtime checks for the legal write.

## Dependencies

Depends on #471; relaxing the diagnostic before packed subpart bounds are preserved can allow writes into a continuously driven neighbor.
title: [IEEE 1800] §6.5 — Accept disjoint mixed-driver packed elements

body:
## Gap

A part-select of a packed element can escape into a neighboring packed element when its base is out of range. A read returns the neighbor's bits rather than X, and a write changes the neighbor.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module t;
  logic [1:0][7:0] words = 16'ha520;
  integer pos = 8;
  initial begin
    words[0][pos +: 4] = 4'hf;
    $display("words=%h", words);
  end
endmodule
```

Expected value remains `16'ha520`; the recorded baseline produces `16'haf20`. A paired read reproducer returns `5` from a neighboring element instead of X. See [DD-022](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-022--packed-subpart-writes-escape-the-selected-element).

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §11.5.1 requires a wholly out-of-range part-select write to have no effect and a partial write to update only in-range bits; reads return X for out-of-range bits.

## Acceptance

- Preserve the bounds of every selected packed carrier for reads and blocking, compound, and nonblocking writes.
- Clip partially out-of-range writes to in-range bits and produce X only for out-of-range read bits.
- Preserve single evaluation of dynamic indices and ascending/descending declarations.
- Add paired tests before relaxing the separate mixed-driver rejection in DD-021.

## Dependencies

Prerequisite for #471. This is distinct from #414's multidimensional bit-select alias case.

## Gap

Some concurrent assertion paths suppress the pass action for vacuous successes. For example, the non-fanout path in the existing recursive-consequent regression sees 17 enabled starts with 16 vacuous successes and one nonvacuous success, but calls the pass action only once. The paired 2017/2023 logs show this is separate from the repaired endpoint aggregation path.

See `tests/sva_recursive_consequent_test.sv` and the paired red logs documented in [DD-005](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-005--non-fanout-assertion-paths-omit-vacuous-user-pass-actions).

## Acceptance

body:
## Gap

Two-state packed reads can return X for invalid selectors, and X bits from a partially out-of-range part-select can survive assignment into a two-state variable. The standard requires 0 for invalid bit-selects on two-state values and converts X/Z to 0 when assigning to a two-state destination.

## Reproducers

```systemverilog
module t;
  bit [7:0] value = '1;
  integer index = 8;
  initial $display("bit_oob=%b", value[index]);
endmodule
```

The current one-dimensional Icarus path prints `bit_oob=x`; IEEE 1800-2017/2023 §11.5.1 requires `0` for this two-state value.

A separate paired reducer in DD-087 uses `bit [99:0] bv = '1; integer b = 96; bit [7:0] br = bv[b +: 8];`. The current result retains `xxxx1111` in `br`; the missing part-select bits must convert to zero on assignment, producing `00001111`.

## IEEE 1800 basis

IEEE 1800-2017 and 1800-2023 §11.5.1 specify invalid bit-select results by source state and require partially out-of-range part-select reads to return X for out-of-range bits. §6.11.2 requires X/Z to become zero when converted to a two-state type.

## Acceptance

- Return 0 for invalid bit-selects on two-state packed values, including unknown and out-of-range indices.
- Convert missing X bits from partially out-of-range part-select reads to zero when the destination is two-state.
- Keep four-state result rules and in-range ascending/descending selections unchanged; add paired 2017/2023 focused cases.
- Record the tested limits in the packed-select matrix.

## Dependencies

None known. This tracks the two-state result/conversion rules and is separate from #414's multidimensional four-state alias and index-boundary case.

## Evidence

See [DD-087](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-087--out-of-range-part-select-of-a-two-state-vector-leaves-x-in-a-two-state-variable) for the paired reducer and logs.

body:
## Gap

Plain escaped macro identifiers are rejected in conditional-compilation directives, although the directive grammar accepts a `text_macro_identifier`, which is a SystemVerilog identifier. The current preprocessor reports `` `ifdef without a macro name`` for the escaped name.

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
`define \foo 1
`ifdef \foo
module escaped_macro_found; endmodule
`else
`error escaped_macro_not_recognized
`endif
```

On a clean source snapshot of `origin/main` at `af89cfc50be1084cc86c48865f3f6ba78d4512fa`, the built `ivlpp` exits with errors at line 2 (`ifdef without a macro name`) and leaves the conditional branches unmatched. The same probe uses a defined escaped macro and has no application dependencies.

## IEEE 1800 basis

IEEE 1800-2017 §22.5 Syntax 22-5 uses `text_macro_identifier` for conditional directives; §5.6 includes escaped identifiers in the SystemVerilog identifier grammar. IEEE 1800-2023 §22.5 likewise defines `text_macro_identifier` as a SystemVerilog identifier, and §5.6 includes escaped identifiers.

## Acceptance

- Accept escaped macro identifiers in `ifdef`, `ifndef`, and `elsif` in both strict 2017 and 2023 modes.
- Add self-authored defined/undefined, branch-selection, and escaped-identifier terminator cases to the preprocessor regressions.
- Preserve existing simple-identifier and macro-expansion behavior; malformed/unterminated escaped identifiers remain diagnostics.
- Record focused test evidence in the conformance matrix.

## Dependencies

None known.

## Scope

IEEE language support only. This is separate from issue #460, which tracks parenthesized Boolean expressions in conditional directives.

body:
## Gap

A function returning an unpacked-array typedef is rejected when used as the subarray value in a nested unpacked-array assignment pattern. The compiler rejects a legal array-valued expression even though direct whole-array function-result assignment works. Implement the nested value path and keep malformed forms as ordinary source diagnostics.

## Current-state probe

Self-authored reducer:

```systemverilog
typedef int pair_t[2];
typedef pair_t pairs_t[2];
function automatic pair_t make_pair(input int base);
  make_pair = '{base, base + 1};
endfunction
pairs_t got;
initial got = '{make_pair(11), make_pair(21)};
```

On clean `origin/main` `af89cfc50be1084cc86c48865f3f6ba78d4512fa` (macOS ARM64), the nested form fails in both `-g2017` and `-g2023` with two elaboration errors: `Expression make_pair(...) is not compatible with this context. Expected array or array-like expression.` It does not ICE. The direct control `pair_t got; got = make_pair(11);` compiles and runs in both editions, printing `got=11,12`. This confirms the reported behavior on the clean baseline. The out-of-tree build used Homebrew Bison 3.8.2 plus explicit libffi/Z3 include and library paths; macOS's default Bison 2.3 fails at `parse.y:2236` before building, which is a local toolchain mismatch rather than a source failure.

The source path is confirmed on clean main. In `PEAssignPattern::elaborate_expr_uarray_()` (`elab_expr.cc`), nested items recurse for `PEAssignPattern` and `PEString`; `PEConcat` and `PEIdent` have dedicated diagnostics; any other non-null child, including a function call, receives the generic incompatible-context error. In VVP, `draw_array_pattern()` (`tgt-vvp/stmt_assign.c`) recurses only for nested `IVL_EX_ARRAY_PATTERN` nodes and otherwise evaluates a leaf according to the target element base type. Whole-RHS unpacked-array function calls take a separate `show_stmt_assign()` path to `draw_ufunc_uarray()` (`tgt-vvp/draw_ufunc.c`), so nested array-return values have no corresponding lowering path. The reproducer therefore reaches a missing elaboration case first, with a second required lowering path for the returned array value.

The older conformance note that direct whole-array function-return assignment is still a graceful `sorry` is stale: the clean-main control compiles and runs in both editions. Correct the matrix to distinguish that supported direct assignment from the still-failing nested pattern form.

## IEEE basis

IEEE 1800-2017 and 1800-2023 §§10.9.1 and 13.4.1. §10.9.1 specifies that array-pattern items are evaluated in the context of assignment to the corresponding element type, with braces matching array dimensions; §13.4.1 allows nonvoid function results in assignments and expressions. The relevant wording is materially the same in both editions.

## Acceptance

- Reproduce the nested-form rejection and direct whole-array control on clean `origin/main` before editing.
- Add self-authored positive, negative, and boundary regressions for nested array-valued function results; register them in both the legacy and JSON runners for each applicable edition.
- Verify and cite the exact IEEE text, then update the clause matrix to correct the stale whole-array-return note and record the tested nested-form boundary.
- Run focused legacy and JSON tests plus neighboring cases.
- Any PR for this issue must target `main` and must not merge until required CI checks pass on that exact PR head.

## Scope

IEEE language/runtime support only. Do not patch OpenTitan or Caliptra application sources as a substitute for compiler behavior.

Source: [current conformance record](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/main/docs/conformance/matrices/ieee1800_2017_clause_matrix.md).
title: [IEEE 1800] §§10.9.1/13.4.1 — Accept array-return values in nested assignment patterns
[IEEE 1800] §11 — Guard each dimension of runtime packed selects

## Current status — 2026-09-14

**Open: native null-input crash reproduced.** Audited against main `9c8f716b1` and its unchanged UVM pin `78c06547a2a0a29b3dc9dcafae62b75b2ff61544`.

The [pinned helper](https://github.com/accellera-official/uvm-core/blob/78c06547a2a0a29b3dc9dcafae62b75b2ff61544/src/dpi/uvm_regex.cc#L240-L290) calls `strlen(re)` before the null check when `deglob == 0`. The [Icarus DPI umbrella](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/9c8f716b1e9005a97e8fc455d5cd463a65646335/uvm_dpi/uvm_dpi_iverilog.cc#L37-L75) still includes that helper. Its `regcomp` wrapper cannot intercept the earlier `strlen` call. Guards in the separate legacy regex entry points do not fix this path.

## Reproduction

A native C++ test of the unmodified pinned `uvm_regex.cc` on macOS produced:

| Call | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `uvm_re_comp(nullptr, 0)` | SIGSEGV (subprocess return code -11) |
| `uvm_re_comp(nullptr, 1)` | Returns null normally (control process exits 0) |

Minimal test:

```cpp
#include "uvm_regex.cc"
int main(int argc, char**) {
    regex_t* result = uvm_re_comp(nullptr, argc > 1);
    if (result) { uvm_re_free(result); return 2; }
    return 0;
}
```

Compile with C++ at `-O0`, the pinned UVM DPI include directory, and installed Icarus headers. On macOS, supply the usual `malloc.h` shim containing `#include <stdlib.h>`. Run without an argument for the crash, and with an argument for the control. Disable core dumps. Tested helper SHA-256: `1109dcc03d008f7124021bc271130a4edd35a34b5950372f48746f446445a61a`.

This reproduces the **native helper boundary**, not an SV-to-DPI null-string path. Reachability through ordinary SystemVerilog string arguments remains unverified. No remote exploit or memory overwrite is claimed.

## Closure requirements

1. Reject null before any length, indexing, or copy operation in the affected native entry path.
2. Add a permanent native regression with the null-regex failure and null-glob control; retain valid and invalid-pattern behavior. Separately establish SV/DPI reachability if claiming a simulator-triggered crash.
3. Review the diagnostic `sprintf` calls for bounded formatting. The original warnings are a hardening concern; the inspected fixed diagnostic messages do not demonstrate a buffer overflow.
4. Preserve the unmodified-UVM policy: use an appropriate upstream dependency update or a reviewed fork-owned boundary fix, rather than an untracked submodule edit. Do not substitute successful regex results for rejected input.

Related but distinct source-only regex edge cases are tracked as [DD-016](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/9c8f716b1e9005a97e8fc455d5cd463a65646335/docs/conformance/DISCOVERED_DEBT.md#dd-016--regex-edge-cases-during-legacy-abi-comparison); this audit does not claim they were reproduced or fixed.

## History

Originally reported from a macOS real-DPI build on 2026-08-10 at the same UVM pin. The September 14 audit confirms the null-regex defect remains; no simulator implementation was changed during issue cleanup.

## FIXED in commit `9f3666d` — m7 now passes

`m7_objection_stress_test` now ends at t=80 and passes; the full UVM suite
is **209 passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped** (m7 un-skipped, KNOWN_FAIL now
empty). ivtest gate: 44 expected, 0 new, 0 stale.

### Root cause (recap)

A reference to `this` (or an enclosing automatic) from a detached
(join_none) fork body nested inside another detached fork resolved to null
for later loop iterations: the forked thread's inherited automatic-context
chain stopped linking back to the owning activation frame across frame
reuse, so `vthread_get_rd_context_item_scoped` walked wt/rd/owned/stacked,
matched nothing for the target scope, and returned a null item. In UVM's
phase hopper this made per-phase `drop_objection` run with `this == null`,
so `get_objection()` returned null and `drop_objection()` silently no-op'd
on the null handle — two phase-hopper objections never dropped and
`run_phases` never returned from `wait_for_objection(UVM_ALL_DROPPED)`.

### Fix

Strictly-additive last-resort fallback in
`vthread_get_rd_context_item_scoped` (`vvp/vthread.cc`): reached only after
every chain walk has already failed (i.e. the read would otherwise be
null), so it cannot alter any currently-resolving case. When the target
automatic scope has exactly one live activation there is no ambiguity, so
it resolves to that activation. Recursive scopes (>1 live context) stay on
the null path.

Regression test: `ivtest/ivltests/sv_this_nested_detached_fork.v`.
Reproducer kept at
`docs/conformance/repros/m7_this_null_nested_detached_fork.sv`.

### Out of scope (separate, pre-existing)

A loop-local captured by a *general inline* detached fork body (not `this`,
and not a task-call argument — #102 handles that) resolves to the scope's
single live frame, i.e. its last value rather than the per-iteration value.
That is a #102-class limitation, not a regression (it was null before), and
would need the general spawn-time closure capture #102 deliberately scoped
out. `this` is unaffected because a non-recursive method has a single live
activation.
title: `this` is null in a nested detached (join_none) fork body → m7 phase-hopper never all-drops

## Fixed in commit `9f1909b` — and NOT the cause of m7

**The fork-capture bug is real and now fixed**, but the earlier claim that
it causes `m7_objection_stress_test` was WRONG. Correcting the record.

### The bug (fixed)

A single-branch `fork task(<automatic>); join_none` re-executed each loop
iteration evaluated the call arguments when the *detached* thread was
scheduled, not at spawn, so inside a class method (single activation
frame) every worker read the loop automatic's final value. IEEE
1800-2017 §9.3.2 requires the value at spawn.

### The fix (correct approach)

The naive "give the loop-body block its own frame" from the first
investigation regresses outer-automatic access (single-task-frame model),
so it was abandoned. The landed fix instead **hoists the callee `%alloc`
+ argument stores to run in the spawning thread, immediately before the
child's `%fork`** (`tgt-vvp/vvp_process.c` `show_stmt_fork` +
`fork_child_hoist_split_`). The callee frame is allocated before the
detach exactly as the fork thread's own frame already is, and the binding
is captured at `%fork` time. Guarded to join_none, single-branch, and the
exact wrapped-auto-call shape, so no other fork form changes.

Verified: `ivtest/ivltests/sv_fork_call_arg_capture.v`; ivtest 44/0/0; UVM
208/0/1.

### Why it is NOT the m7 cause (corrected)

m7's phase hopper captures its per-phase handle with an **inline**
declaration initializer (`fork automatic uvm_phase phase = ph; begin
process_phase(phase); drop_objection(phase); end join_none`), and that
form **already captured correctly** at baseline (a fork-scope automatic
initialized from an outer var gets per-spawn storage). Confirmed with a
reduced repro. The m7 workers' `fork worker(phase, idx); join_none` *was*
subject to this bug, but only mis-timed `idx` (all fired at t=80); the
objection *counts* stayed balanced. With the fix applied, m7 still fails
identically (`t=9200`), so the phase-hopper objection off-by-two on
`uvm_top` (27 raises / 25 drops) is a **separate, still-unidentified
issue**, not fork capture. Tracked separately; the m7 KNOWN_FAIL comment
is being corrected to stop blaming this bug.
title: Per-iteration `automatic` local captured by join_none fork shares one slot inside a class method

## Not a bug — correct static-initialization ordering

On re-investigation this is **correct SystemVerilog behavior**, not a
defect. My reproducer conflated static-initialization order with a copy
failure.

`C e = new c;` where `e` is a *static* variable (the default) is a static
variable initializer. Per IEEE 1800-2017 §6.21, static initializers run
**before time zero**, before any `initial`/`always` process executes. In
the reproducer, `c.n = 42` (or `c.f()`) is a *procedural* statement that
runs at time 0. So the static initializer `new c` copies `c` while `c.n`
is still 0 — the pre-write value — which is exactly what a conforming
simulator does. iverilog even warns: "Static variable initialization
requires explicit lifetime in this context."

The netlist is correct: the `<shallow_copy>` node carries `c` as its
source operand; it simply executes in the static-init phase.

Verification — making the initializer procedural (an `automatic` variable
or a variable inside an automatic task) copies the post-write value as
expected:

```systemverilog
task automatic run();
  C c = new; c.n = 42;
  begin C e = new c; $display("%0d", e.n); end   // prints 42 (automatic → procedural init)
endtask
```

```
auto decl n=42
```

The statement form `d = new c;` also runs procedurally and copies 42.
Both correct. Closing as not-planned (invalid). The #100 fix and its
test are unaffected — the test already uses the procedural statement form.
title: Copy constructor as a declaration initializer (`C d = new src;`) does not copy

## Fixed in commit `def61d5`

Real/string class-property unpacked arrays now have per-element storage.

**Storage** (`vvp/class_type.cc`): `property_real<T>` and
`property_string` carry an `array_size_` (mirroring
`property_object`/`property_atom`); `instance_size`, `construct`,
`destruct`, and `copy` iterate every element; indexed
`set_real`/`get_real`/`set_string`/`get_string` overrides added. Base
`class_property_t` gains indexed real/string virtuals that default to the
scalar path. `configure_property` passes the array size through.
`class_type` and `vvp_cobject` accessors take an element index (default
0); the indexed `set_val`/`get_from_obj` helpers forward it.

**Opcodes**: `%store/prop/r/i`, `%store/prop/str/i`, `%prop/r/i`,
`%prop/str/i` (`vvp/codes.h`, `compile.cc`, `vthread.cc`). Each peeks the
object (no pop), so a whole-array pattern stores every element under one
push.

**Codegen** (`tgt-vvp`): `stmt_assign.c` real/string property branches
handle an element index (`obj.arr[i] = ...`) and whole-array patterns
(`obj.arr = '{...}`); `eval_real.c`/`eval_string.c` read `obj.arr[i]` via
`%prop/{r,str}/i`.

**Verified** in `ivtest/ivltests/sv_class_prop_real_string_array.v`:
element-wise write, whole-array pattern, variable-index read/write,
scalar-property regression, shallow copy. ivtest gate: 44 expected, 0
new, 0 stale. UVM: 208 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped.

Note: the shallow-copy check uses the statement form (`d = new c`). The
declaration-initializer form `C d = new c;` copies nothing — a separate
pre-existing bug filed as #101.
title: Class-property unpacked array of real/string stores every element to the same slot

## Update 2026-07-21 — compiler crash fixed; full support still open

The **compiler abort is resolved** in commit `0d6a9c9`. Assigning an
unpacked-array-returning function as a whole array now emits a clean
`sorry` diagnostic with file/line instead of aborting with the internal
assertion `store_vec4_to_lval: lwid == ivl_signal_width(lsig)`:

```
foo.v:5: sorry: a function that returns an unpacked array cannot yet be
assigned to an unpacked array; the vvp calling convention has no
unpacked-array return path.
```

The guard (`PAssign::elaborate`, netuarray l-value branch) detects a
uarray-returning `NetEUFunc` r-value and covers 1-D, multidimensional,
and delayed forms. CE test `ivtest/ivltests/sv_uarray_func_return_fail.v`
verifies a clean compile error and no core dump.

**Still open (this issue):** actual support for unpacked-array function
return values. The root cause is that the vvp calling convention has no
unpacked-array return path — `%callf/{void,vec4,real,str,obj}` deliver
only scalars, packed vectors, reals, strings, and object handles. Real
support needs either:

1. a new array-return mechanism (e.g. `%callf/arr` plus a runtime
   array-copy of the callee's return signal into the caller's array), or
2. lowering the array return through an implicit output-ref parameter so
   the callee writes directly into the caller's array.

Until then the feature stays DIAGNOSED, not FULL. The original
diagnosis below stands, except that the return *type* is elaborated
correctly (a `netuarray_t`) — the earlier note about `bool[0:2] width=1`
was the stub renderer's degenerate display of a uarray, not the actual
signal type. The gap is the calling convention, not type fidelity.
title: Unpacked-array typedef as a function return type loses its element type (ivl crash)

body:
## Context

With per-instance class events now correct (PR #96), the UVM objection front door no longer cross-wakes. This un-masks a separate, pre-existing gap in objection **count** propagation that the shared-event cross-wake had been hiding.

## Symptom

`tests/m7_objection_stress_test.sv` (8 concurrent workers holding the run-phase objection until t=80, plus a child with an explicit count) against unmodified UVM 2020.3.1:

- The objection **counters** pass (`workers=8 child_drops=3`).
- But the run does **not** end at t=80 — it extends to the UVM 9200 s watchdog, so the end-of-sim time check fails.

The test completes (no wall-clock hang); it is on the harness `KNOWN_FAIL` list for this reason.

## Root cause (instrumented)

The `uvm_phase_hopper`'s `phase_hopper_objection` is raised on `uvm_phase` keys (`try_put` → `raise_objection(phase, ...)`) and the hopper waits on `wait_for_objection(UVM_ALL_DROPPED)` = `wait_for(UVM_ALL_DROPPED, uvm_root)`.

Instrumenting `uvm_objection::all_dropped` and `wait_for` shows, for the `phase_hopper_objection` instance:

```
DBG WAIT all_dropped objn=<hopper> key=uvm_root
DBG all_dropped ENTRY objn=<hopper> key=<component_1> exists=0
DBG all_dropped ENTRY objn=<hopper> key=<component_2> exists=0
...            (many component/phase keys)
# but NEVER: all_dropped ENTRY objn=<hopper> key=uvm_root
```

So the hopper objection's `all_dropped` fires for every component/phase key as they drop, but is **never called for `uvm_root`** — its integer `m_total_count[uvm_root]` never returns to 0. Therefore the hopper's `@(m_events[uvm_root].all_dropped)` never wakes, `run_phases` never returns, and phasing only ends at the watchdog.

In the shared-event baseline this was masked: a *different* objection instance's `all_dropped` trigger cross-woke the hopper's waiter (1 trigger → 2 wakes), so the phase advanced anyway (prematurely — which is why the post-run function phases were documented as never executing).

## Expected behavior

When all phases have been processed and their hopper objections dropped, `phase_hopper_objection`'s `uvm_root` count reaches 0, `all_dropped(uvm_root)` fires, `run_phases` returns, and the run ends cleanly (≈ t=80 in this test), with the post-run function phases (extract/check/report/final) executing.

## Likely subsystem

UVM objection count propagation to `m_top` for a `uvm_phase`-keyed objection — `m_propagate` / `m_drop` / `m_forked_drain` climbing the hierarchy from a non-component key up to `uvm_root`. Needs a reduced pure-SV reproducer of the phase-keyed propagation to isolate whether a drop is lost or the climb terminates early.

## Severity

P0 (UVM semantic blocker) — this is the remaining blocker for full extract/check/report/final phase execution in M7.

## Related

- PR #96 (per-instance class events) fixes the language-level half.
- `docs/conformance/session_logs/2026-07-21_per_instance_class_events.md` has the instrumented evidence.
- `docs/conformance/m7_stress_findings_2026-07-18.md` (Finding 1) documents the original masked behavior.
title: UVM phase_hopper_objection never all-drops to the top under concurrent objection traffic (blocks clean run_phase completion)

## Reproducer

```systemverilog
module m;
  class c; int id; endclass
  c arr[2];
  initial begin
    arr[0] = new;
    arr[0].id = 5;             // <-- crashes ivl
    $display("%0d", arr[0].id);
    $finish(0);
  end
endmodule
```

```
$ iverilog -g2012 -o /dev/null t.sv
ivl: t-dll-api.cc:817: ivl_variable_type_t ivl_expr_value(ivl_expr_t): Assertion `net' failed.
Aborted
```

Both a constant index (`arr[0].id`) and a variable/loop index (`arr[i].id`) crash. Reading (`arr[0].id` on the RHS) is fine; only the **store** crashes.

## Expected behavior

Legal SystemVerilog: assign `5` to the `id` property of the object held in `arr[0]`. Should compile and run, printing `5`.

## Actual behavior

Compiler (ivl) aborts on an assertion. Crashing, not silent.

## IEEE clause

8 (classes) / 7.4 (unpacked arrays) — property lvalue of an array-of-handles element.

## Likely subsystem

tgt-vvp code generation. Backtrace:

```
#7  ivl_expr_value (net=0x0) at t-dll-api.cc:817
#8  draw_eval_expr_into_integer (expr=0x0, ix=4) at eval_expr.c:298
#9  show_stmt_assign_sig_cobject (net=...) at stmt_assign.c:2472
#10 show_stmt_assign (net=...) at stmt_assign.c:2514
```

`show_stmt_assign_sig_cobject` calls `draw_eval_expr_into_integer` with a NULL index expression when the cobject lvalue is itself an element of an array (the element-index expression is not being threaded through).

## Severity

P1 — compiler crash on legal SystemVerilog.

## Notes

Pre-existing; discovered while testing per-instance class events (PR #96), but entirely unrelated to events — the reproducer above uses no events. The array-of-object property-store lvalue path in `stmt_assign.c` needs to supply the element index to `draw_eval_expr_into_integer` (and handle the NULL case) rather than passing a null expression.
title: ivl crash: store to a property of an unpacked-array-of-class element (arr[i].prop = expr)

## Current status — 2026-09-14

**Open: fresh performance baseline required.** This issue is an assessment task until the current OpenTitan UART workload has been reproduced and profiled. There is no current measurement establishing either the old bottleneck diagnosis or its resolution.

The [July 28 review](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/issues/46#issuecomment-5105796072) already warned that relevant scheduler/container code had changed. The [September 13 application census](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/9c8f716b1e9005a97e8fc455d5cd463a65646335/docs/conformance/session_logs/2026-09-13_opentitan_caliptra_rebaseline_after277.md) is compatibility evidence at `631bba6e8`, not a controlled UART performance benchmark. A timeout becoming a runtime failure is not a speedup claim.

## Next action

1. Pin the current compiler/runtime revision, unmodified OpenTitan and UVM revisions, top/test, seed, flags, host, and resource limits. Record exact commands and tool fingerprints.
2. Establish meaningful traffic, expected checking, and normal completion. If correctness, setup, or dependency failures prevent a valid baseline, record the blocker; do not count a shorter failed run as faster simulation.
3. Measure repeated runs and report simulated time, wall time, CPU time, and the median simulation/wall-time rate. Profile the current hot path before proposing an optimization.
4. Use the measurements to decide whether a concrete optimization ticket is warranted. Close this assessment with evidence if no actionable bottleneck remains; otherwise link a narrowly scoped follow-up with its measured target and correctness gates.

Any implementation must preserve IEEE event ordering and observable behavior and pass the affected regression gates. The [blocker registry](https://github.com/dsellerbrock/iverilog-uvm/blob/9c8f716b1e9005a97e8fc455d5cd463a65646335/docs/conformance/BLOCKERS.md) and active-work workflow own implementation selection.

## Historical targets — not current measurements

The original Phase 61/74 report cited roughly 244 ns of simulated time per wall-clock second and about two hours for a 2 ms UART smoke. It proposed a 5× improvement / 5 ms within 30 minutes and a `96+/98` regression threshold. These figures are retained for context; they are not a validated baseline or today's regression requirement.

The original candidate changes—lock-free queues, anyedge batching, small-map fast paths, and instruction-cache warmup—were hypotheses. The old requirement to implement at least two is replaced by profiling and the smallest justified fix. No particular data structure or scheduler rewrite is preselected.

No fresh UART benchmark was run during this issue audit. The issue is not marked fixed or duplicated.
title: Rebaseline OpenTitan UART performance before optimizing VVP

## Summary

A class property `cfg` reads non-null at the start of a method but reads null some simulated time later within the same method, causing `%wait/vif/posedge: object is not a virtual interface (nil=1, cobject=(nil))` and a vvp core dump.

## Repro (in OpenTitan UART DV after Phases 50/54/55/56 land)

\`tl_host_driver::a_channel_thread\` traces:
\`\`\`
[ACT] a_channel_thread start \$time=811000 ps cfg=non-null
[WCR] cfg=null at \$time=831000 ps
%wait/vif/posedge: object is not a virtual interface (nil=1, cobject=(nil), raw=(nil))
vvp: vthread.cc:13816: bool of_WAIT_VIF_POSEDGE(...): Assertion 'vif' failed.
\`\`\`

Between `[ACT]` (entry of `a_channel_thread`) and `[WCR]` (entry of `wait_clk_or_rst`, called from a_channel_thread), 20 ns of simulated time passes and `cfg` (the driver's `tl_agent_cfg cfg` member) becomes null.

There is no explicit assignment to `cfg` in the path. The property is presumably being misread after some control-flow boundary (likely a fork or DV_SPINWAIT_EXIT).

## Suggested approach

1. Build a focused reproducer: a class with a class-typed property `cfg`, a method `outer()` calling `inner()` via a fork, and a fork-internal `@()` that delays. Inspect whether `this.cfg` reads null after the delay.
2. Look at how `this` and class-property reads are preserved through `%fork` / `DV_SPINWAIT_EXIT` / `disable fork`.
3. Compare with prior fork-related fixes (Phase 37 mutual recursion, Phase 50 deferred body elaboration, Phase 50e pre/post hooks).

## Related

- Blocked by #29 (wait sensitivity through vif) — once that lands, the OT fork on tl_monitor can be reverted and the cfg-null pattern can be re-traced cleanly.
- Likely blocks completion of UART DV smoke test.

## OpenTitan impact

After Phase 50d/e/f + Phase 54 + Phase 55 + Phase 56 land, the UART DV simulation reaches `uart_smoke_vseq starting run 1/2 / begin sending 5 rx bytes` (sim time ~810 ms). Then this issue causes a vvp core dump.
title: Phase 60: Class-property handle (cfg) reads null mid-method execution

body:
## Summary

`seq_item_port.try_next_item(req)` falls through to the `uvm_sqr_if_base::try_next_item` error stub instead of dispatching virtually to the sequencer's override:

```
UVM_ERROR @ ... [try_next_item] Sequencer interface task not implemented
```

## OpenTitan impact

`tl_host_driver::a_channel_thread` calls `seq_item_port.try_next_item(req)` to non-blockingly check the sequencer for items. With the dispatch broken, `req` stays null, the inner forever loop just spins, and the driver never actually pulls items from the sequencer. Combined with #30 (cfg=null) this leads to a `%wait/vif/posedge` assertion crash.

## Root cause

The dispatch chain:
- `seq_item_port` is a `uvm_seq_item_pull_port`
- It forwards to `m_imp.try_next_item(t)` where `m_imp` is the connected sequencer
- The sequencer is `uvm_sequencer #(REQ, RSP)` extending `uvm_seq_item_pull_imp` (defines `try_next_item` via the `UVM_SEQ_ITEM_PULL_IMP` macro)
- The base class `uvm_sqr_if_base::try_next_item` is the always-error stub at `accellera-official.uvm-core/src/tlm1/uvm_sqr_ifs.svh:99`

If iverilog's virtual method dispatch through the parameterized `uvm_seq_item_pull_imp` doesn't reach the sequencer's override, we hit the base stub.

## Suggested approach

Likely the same family as Phase 50 (parameterized class indexed-vif method dispatch through fork). The macro `UVM_SEQ_ITEM_PULL_IMP(m_imp, REQ, RSP, t, t)` expands to virtual task overrides on a parameterized class. iverilog's virtual table lookup may not find these when called through the port-imp chain.

Steps:
1. Build a focused reproducer: a parameterized port + parameterized imp + simple class dispatch chain (mirror of `uvm_seq_item_pull_port` → `uvm_seq_item_pull_imp` → user sequencer).
2. Trace where the dispatch lands — likely the `class_type->resolve_method_call_scope` or virtual-dispatch lookup misses the override.
3. Compare with how Phase 50 fixed similar parameterized-class dispatch issues.

## Related

- Blocked by #29 (cfg=null) — fixing #29 may expose more of this.
- Phase 50 / Phase 54 are reference points for parameterized class method dispatch fixes.
title: Phase 59: UVM port-imp virtual dispatch (seq_item_port.try_next_item)

body:
## Summary

`wait(<vif-chain-expr>)` doesn't trigger when the underlying virtual-interface signal changes, because `nex_input` on a `NetEProperty` chain returns the root `this` nexus rather than the iface signal.

## Repro

`tests/wait_vif_isunknown_test.sv` (in the dev-branch test suite) — a `Watcher` class with `virtual my_if vif`, calling `wait(!\$isunknown(vif.rst_n))`. The wait never fires even after the testbench drives `iface.rst_n = 1`.

```sv
class Watcher;
  virtual my_if vif;
  task watch();
    wait(!\$isunknown(vif.rst_n));   // <-- never wakes
  endtask
endclass
```

## OpenTitan impact

`tl_monitor::monitor_reset` in OT uses:
```sv
wait(!\$isunknown(cfg.vif.rst_n));
forever wait(cfg.vif.rst_n != !cfg.in_reset);
```

Both block forever. `cfg.in_reset` stays stuck at 1 from time 0, every `tl_host_driver` request goes down the abort path, and `csr_wr` returns `UVM_NOT_OK`. Worked around in OT fork via `@(cfg.vif.rst_n)` edge events (see opentitan iverilog-uvm branch commit 3416154).

## Root cause

Pinpointed in `iverilog/net_nex_input.cc:171-174`:
```cpp
if (const NetExpr*base = get_base()) {
    delete result;
    result = base->nex_input();
}
```

For a chain like `vif.rst_n` (`NetEProperty(rst_n) over NetEProperty(vif) over NetESignal(this)`), recursion through `get_base()` reduces the result to the `this` nexus — the class handle, which never changes. The wait probe is therefore connected to a never-changing nexus and the wait while-loop never re-evaluates.

## Existing infrastructure

- The `%wait/vif/anyedge` runtime opcode exists (`vthread.cc:13843, of_WAIT_VIF_ANYEDGE`). It pops a vif, gets its anyedge functor, and registers the thread on the wait list. This is what `@(vif.sig)` already uses.
- `NetEvProbe::set_vif_anyedge(N, M, pre_N)` is the netlist-level marker. `tgt-vvp/vvp_process.c:1723` consumes it and emits `%wait/vif/anyedge`.
- The path is fully wired for `@(vif edge)` events. The gap is `wait()`-loop elaboration: it builds a `NetWhile(cond, NetEvWait(NetEvent))` where `NetEvent` is signal-driven, not vif-aware.

## Suggested approach

Make `PEventStatement::elaborate_wait` (elaborate.cc:7397) detect when the wait expression contains a virtual-interface signal chain. When it does, replace the standard `NetEvWait(signal-driven NetEvent)` with a `NetEvWait` whose probe carries `set_vif_anyedge(N, M, pre_N)`. The existing tgt-vvp path for `@(vif)` events emits `%wait/vif/anyedge`; reuse it.

The current `try_set_vif_anyedge` lambda at line 7570+ already finds vif chains for `@()` events but only sets a flag that's never consumed for the `wait()` path. Wire that flag through `NetEvWait` → `NetEvent` so `tgt-vvp/vvp_process.c:show_stmt_wait` recognizes vif-aware NetEvWaits and emits `%wait/vif/anyedge` instead of the regular `%wait E_*`.

## Validation

1. `tests/wait_vif_isunknown_test.sv` — `reached_known=1` after testbench drives rst_n.
2. Revert OT workaround at `hw/dv/sv/tl_agent/tl_monitor.sv` (restore `wait(!\$isunknown(...))` and `wait(rst_n != !in_reset)`); UART DV should still get past the reset deassertion check.

## Related

- Blocks #29 #30 — `cfg=null` and `try_next_item` issues are downstream of this.
- This was the workaround target in OT commit `3416154`.
title: Phase 58: wait()-loop sensitivity through virtual-interface signal chain

body:
## Status

The OpenTitan UART DV testbench now **compiles to a VVP file with 0 elaboration errors and 0 code-generation errors** (using `-DSYNTHESIS` + `-DUVM_NO_DPI`). The simulation runs but hits runtime errors that prevent UVM test execution from completing.

## What was fixed to get to zero compile errors

- Complex event expressions in auto tasks → SV-mode `continue` (compile-progress)
- `NetEScope` used as event expression (clocking block) → caught and skipped
- `NetEProperty::synthesize()` → silent null override (prevents double error count)
- Empty event wait (`wa->nevents()==0`) → `set_t0_trigger()` for non-auto, return body for auto
- NB assignment in function → actually create `NetAssign` (blocking) in SV mode
- `elab_lval.cc` compile-progress path → return null instead of invalid nested lval
- `stmt_assign.c` compound string assignment assert → compile-progress skip
- `eval_expr.c` wide-constant assert → truncate-to-zero fallback
- `draw_net_input.c` uwire multi-driver error → downgrade to warning (treat as TRI)
- `vpi/sys_icarus.c` → add real `$system()` implementation

## Runtime errors (blocking test execution)

### 1. `$value$plusargs` with class property / constant args

The most frequent blocker. OpenTitan DV passes class properties or string constants as the destination argument:

```
ERROR: dv_lib/dv_base_test.sv:79:   $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiConstant.
ERROR: dv_lib/dv_base_test.sv:91:   $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
ERROR: alert_esc_agent.sv:63:       $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
ERROR: cip_base_vseq.sv:469:        $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
ERROR: dv_report_server.sv:17:      $value$plusargs's second argument must be a variable, found a vpiClassVar.
```

**Fix needed**: In `vpi/sys_vcsuser.c` `$value$plusargs` implementation — accept `vpiClassVar` destination using `vpi_put_value()`, and silently skip (no match) for `vpiConstant`.

### 2. `$sformatf` type 116 (class object)

```
ERROR: cip_base_scoreboard.sv:589: $sformatf does not support argument type (116).
```

Type 116 = `vpiClassObj`. When `%0s` or `%p` is used with a class handle, the formatter falls through with no handler.

**Fix needed**: In `vpi/sys_display.c` — add a case for `vpiClassObj` that emits `<object:0xADDR>` or calls the object's `convert2string()` if available.

### 3. Unresolved functor stubs

```
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfcba9c20_0; created placeholder net
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfd2a4920_0; created placeholder net
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfd4132e0_0; created placeholder net
unresolved functor stub: v0x60bbfd453dd0_0; created placeholder net
unresolved vpi name lookup: v0x60bbfd54fb50_0; using null handle
```

These are likely struct/packed-array output ports on RTL modules (TL-UL signals) whose synthesis emitted stub labels that weren't resolved. The VPI handle lookup then gets a null.

**Fix needed**: Investigate which RTL struct ports produce these stubs; may require fixing packed struct output port synthesis in `draw_net_input.c` or `vvp_process.c`.

### 4. Callf async warning (secondary)

```
Warning: callf child did not end synchronously (caller=uvm_pkg::_ivl_276.m_register_pair callee=...get); caller entering join wait
```

UVM internal pair registration hits the async callf path. Non-fatal but indicates a phase-execution gap.

## Suggested fix priority

1. `$value$plusargs` vpiClassVar — most frequent, blocks build phase config
2. `$value$plusargs` vpiConstant — silently no-op
3. `$sformatf` type 116 — formatting only
4. Unresolved functor stubs — RTL investigation needed

## Reproduction

```sh
ulimit -v 3000000
# compile (0 errors)
iverilog -g2012 -DSYNTHESIS -DUVM_NO_DPI \
  -I accellera-official.uvm-core/src \
  -I opentitan/hw/ip/uart/dv/env \
  ... (full dep list in memory/project_opentitan_uart.md) \
  -o /tmp/uart_dv.vvp \
  accellera-official.uvm-core/src/uvm_pkg.sv \
  ... (RTL + DV files)
# run (shows runtime errors)
vvp /tmp/uart_dv.vvp
```
title: OpenTitan UART DV: VVP generates (0 errors), runtime stubs needed

## Summary

Two pre-existing TLM failures that prevent real driver/sequence testbenches from working:

### 1. Sequencer/driver handshake (`seq_trace_test.sv`)

`seq_item_port.get_next_item(item)` spins infinitely with `UVM_ERROR [get_next_item] Sequencer interface task not implemented`.

The port's `m_if` (set during `resolve_bindings`) is either null or not resolved to the correct IMP. Virtual dispatch on `m_if.get_next_item()` falls to the `uvm_sqr_if_base` base class stub, which returns immediately — causing the driver loop to spin forever.

The `tlm_debug_test` (blocking_put_port) works correctly, so basic TLM port dispatch is functional. The issue is specific to `uvm_seq_item_pull_port` / `uvm_seq_item_pull_imp` — the parameterized sequencer IMP combination. The IMP's `get_next_item` at `TD_uvm_pkg._ivl_341.get_next_item` exists in the VVP but is never dispatched to.

### 2. Analysis port subscriber write (`analysis_test.sv`)

`ap.write(t)` in a monitor does not reach the subscriber's `write(t)` method. The same `m_if` / TLM resolve_bindings issue likely applies to `uvm_analysis_port`.

## Root cause hypothesis

`uvm_port_base::resolve_bindings()` does not correctly populate `m_imp_list` for the parameterized sequencer IMP, leaving `m_if = null`. Without a valid `m_if`, the virtual dispatch in `get_next_item` reads null from `@` and falls to the base class stub.

The `uvm_blocking_put_port` works because its IMP registration path is simpler (no 3-level parameterization with `this_type`).

## Investigation notes

- VVP label `TD_uvm_pkg._ivl_341.get_next_item` exists — the IMP implementation is compiled correctly
- The `connect()` call in `connect_phase` appears to reach the IMP (property 58 of `sqr`)
- Dispatch trace (`IVL_VDISPATCH_TRACE=1`) shows the failure happens before `run_phase` can be reached in 2-second window
- Pre-Phase-3 binary and pre-Phase-3 VVP both fail identically — confirmed pre-existing

## Files to investigate

- `vvp/vthread.cc` — `maybe_dispatch_virtual_method_call_`, look for why `m_if` is null
- `vvp/vvp_cobject.cc` — associative map (`Mo`) property access for `m_imp_list`
- `accellera-official.uvm-core/src/base/uvm_port_base.svh` — `resolve_bindings`, `m_add_list`, `set_if`

## Blocks

This blocks all real driver/sequence testbenches. Should be fixed before Phase 4 (register layer), which requires a working sequencer.
title: Phase 1d: Sequencer/driver TLM dispatch and analysis port write

## Summary

Two Phase 2 randomization features were deferred after `rand_mode()` was implemented. Both require additions to the Z3 constraint solving pipeline.

## constraint_mode(name, 0/1)

Per-constraint enable/disable:

```systemverilog
class my_item;
  rand int addr;
  constraint c_addr { addr inside {[0:255]}; }
  
  task body();
    c_addr.constraint_mode(0);  // disable — currently silently ignored
    item.randomize();
    c_addr.constraint_mode(1);  // re-enable
  endtask
endclass
```

**Implementation plan:**
- Add `constraint_mode_` bool map (by name) to `class_type` in VVP (`class_type.h/cc`)
- `%constraint_mode name, 0/1` opcode to set it (like `%rand_mode`)
- `of_RANDOMIZE` / Z3 solver: skip constraints where `constraint_mode_[name] = false`
- Elaborate: `constraint_mode(name, en)` → `$ivl_class_method$constraint_mode` NetSTask
- tgt-vvp: emit name string + mode value + `%constraint_mode`

## dist weighted distributions

```systemverilog
rand int val;
constraint c { val dist { 0 := 10, [1:9] := 70, 10 := 20 }; }
```

**Implementation plan:**
- New IR node: `(dist p:N:W [(c:V w:W) ...] [(c:lo:hi w:W) ...])` 
- Z3: implement as weighted random selection — pick a bin first (proportional to weight), then pick value within range, then run constraint check
- Parse.y: `dist` expression grammar → `PEDist` AST node
- Elaborate: `pexpr_to_constraint_ir()` handles `PEDist`

## Priority

These are correctness features for advanced constrained-random tests. Recommend implementing after Phase 3 and Phase 4 are complete.
title: Phase 2 (deferred): constraint_mode() and dist weighted distributions

## Key capabilities needed

### Covergroups

- [ ] Sequence operators: `##`, `|->`, `|=>`, `[*]`, `[->]`

## Current state

iverilog has partial SystemVerilog assertion support but the VVP runtime coverage collection is not wired to UVM's coverage database.

## Summary

The UVM register layer (`uvm_reg_block`, `uvm_reg`, `uvm_reg_map`, `uvm_reg_sequence`) is required for any testbench that verifies hardware registers via a bus interface.

## Key capabilities needed

- [ ] `uvm_reg_block` instantiation and `create_map` / `add_reg`
- [ ] `uvm_reg::write()` / `uvm_reg::read()` task calls through the bus adapter
- [ ] `uvm_reg_frontdoor` and adapter sequence mechanism
- [ ] `uvm_reg_predictor` / register mirror model
- [ ] `uvm_reg_sequence` integration

## Current state

Several `uvm_reg_frontdoor` methods are compile-progress stubs (silently ignored):
- `start` task in `uvm_mem.svh:1328`
- Reg layer method stubs via `is_uvm_compile_progress`

## Prerequisites

- Phase 3 (virtual interface) should be complete — bus adapters typically use VIF
- Phase 2 rand constraints may be needed for constrained register sequences

## Notes

The register layer is large (~10K lines in UVM source). Recommend starting with a minimal `write/read` path through a direct `uvm_reg_adapter` before tackling the full predictor/mirror model.
title: Phase 4: UVM register layer (uvm_reg, uvm_reg_block)

## Summary

Virtual interfaces used as class members are a fundamental pattern in UVM testbenches:

```systemverilog
class my_driver extends uvm_driver;
  virtual simple_if vif;
  task run_phase(uvm_phase phase);
    @(posedge vif.clk);   // <-- currently: wait on 'this', hangs
    vif.data = 8'hAB;
  endtask
endclass
```

## Status

**`@(posedge vif.clk)` — DONE** (commit 98895080a). The elaborator detects the 3-level `NetEProperty` chain, emits `%wait/vif/posedge M`, and the VVP runtime lazily connects a `vvp_fun_edge_sa` to the actual signal inside the `vvp_vinterface`.

## Remaining work

- [ ] `@(negedge vif.clk)` — same pipeline, add `%wait/vif/negedge M`  
- [ ] `@(vif.clk)` (any-edge) — `%wait/vif/anyedge M`
- [ ] Assign to vif member `vif.data = val` from class context (currently works via `set_vec4` if VVP is correct; needs elaboration wiring verification)
- [ ] Read from vif member `val = vif.data` (same)
- [ ] Multiple virtual interface members in one class
- [ ] Passing vif via `uvm_config_db #(virtual simple_if)::set/get`
- [ ] Virtual interface ports in modules connected to class members

## Test

`tests/vif_probe.sv` — drives data=0xAB after posedge and asserts valid. Currently PASSED.
title: Phase 3 (in progress): Virtual interface as class member — full support
